(3.90)

which are denoted as

(D_{1}^{\omega^{i}}\,,\mathcal{O}^{i,j})=\left((D_{1}^{\omega^{i}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{i})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,j}\right)\,,\qquad i,j=1,2\,.

(3.91)

The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
acts on end of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
as
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\leftrightarrow\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}
and therefore acts on the twisted sector operators as

D_{2}^{b}:\quad\mathcal{O}^{i,j}\longleftrightarrow\mathcal{O}^{[i+1]_{2},j}\,.

(3.92)

These operators decompose into two disjoint sets that are
\mathcal{O}^{i,i}
and
\mathcal{O}^{i,[j+1]_{2}}
.
Operators in these sets are mutually orthogonal i.e.

\mathcal{O}^{i,i}\mathcal{O}^{i,[j+1]_{2}}=0\,,

(3.93)

and can normalized to satisfy the algebra

\begin{split}\mathcal{O}^{1,1}\mathcal{O}^{2,2}=v_{0}\,,\qquad\mathcal{O}^{1,1}\mathcal{O}^{1,1}=\mathcal{O}^{2,2}\,,\qquad\mathcal{O}^{2,2}\mathcal{O}^{2,2}=\mathcal{O}^{1,1}\,,\\
\mathcal{O}^{1,2}\mathcal{O}^{2,1}=v_{1}\,,\qquad\mathcal{O}^{1,2}\mathcal{O}^{1,2}=\mathcal{O}^{2,1}\,,\qquad\mathcal{O}^{2,1}\mathcal{O}^{2,1}=\mathcal{O}^{1,2}\,.\\
\end{split}

(3.94)

From this it is clear that
\mathcal{O}^{1,1}
and
\mathcal{O}^{2,2}
trivialize the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry within the vacuum
v_{0}
, meanwhile
\mathcal{O}^{1,2}
and
\mathcal{O}^{2,1}
trivialize the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry within
v_{1}
.
As required by consistency with the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
action, we have

D_{2}^{b}:(v_{0},\mathcal{O}^{1,1}\,,\mathcal{O}^{2,2})\longleftrightarrow(v^{1},\mathcal{O}^{2,1}\,,\mathcal{O}^{1,2})\,.

(3.95)

Therefore the resulting gapped phase can be summarized as as a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
-SSB with 1-form symmetry
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
preserved in each vacuum, i.e. a confining phase:

2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
SSB
\boxtimes

{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
Trivial (Confining Phase)

(3.96)

3.4.2
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
SSB Phase

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}),p^{\prime}}\,.

(3.97)

The order parameters carry the generalized charges
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
in the corresponding gapped phase.
As in the previous section,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
can end on both the physical and symmetry boundary and therefore becomes a topological
local operator
\mathcal{O}^{P}
after compactifying the SymTFT.

(3.98)

There are no additional local operators and therefore we obtain two vacua
v_{0}
and
v_{1}
as in (
3.88
) which are exchanged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry.

Next, the surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
can also end on untwisted sector lines both the physical and symmetry boundary.
We denote its ends on the physical boundary as
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{a}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{a^{2}}
and on the symmetry boundary as
{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{a}
and
{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{a^{2}}
.

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
surface extended between both boundaries, one gets four lines as

(3.99)

which are denoted as

\mathcal{L}^{j,k}=({\mathcal{E}}^{a^{j}}_{1}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}^{a^{k}}_{1})\,,\qquad j,k=1,2\,.

(3.100)

The lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{j}}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{a^{j}}
at the ends of
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
on the two boundaries satisfy the fusion rules and F-symbols in (
4.46
)
3
3

3

The relations satisfied by
\mathcal{L}_{i}
are obtained by replacing
p
with
-p^{\prime}
in (
4.46
).

\begin{split}\mathcal{E}_{1}^{j}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{j}&=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[j+1]_{2}}\,,\qquad\mathcal{E}_{1}^{j}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[j+1]_{2}}=D_{1}^{\omega^{p}}\,,\\
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{j}\otimes\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{j}&=\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[j+1]_{2}}\,,\qquad\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{j}\otimes\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[j+1]_{2}}=D_{1}^{\omega^{p^{\prime}}}\,.\end{split}

(3.101)

Using these and consistency with the bulk fusion of

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
, we obtain the following fusion rules for
\mathcal{L}^{j,k}
.

\mathcal{L}^{j,j}\mathcal{L}^{[j+1]_{2},j}=0\,,\qquad\mathcal{L}^{j,j}\mathcal{L}^{j,[j+1]_{2}}=0\,.

(3.102)

The lines therefore decompose into two sets
\{\mathcal{L}^{1,1},\mathcal{L}^{2,2}\}
and
\{\mathcal{L}^{1,2},\mathcal{L}^{2,1}\}
that have vanishing fusion product among them.
These sets of lines are exchanged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry and act on distinct vacua of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
SSB phase.
Without loss of generality, we may assume that
\{\mathcal{L}^{1,1}\,,\mathcal{L}^{2,2}\}
act within the vacuum
v_{0}
while
\{\mathcal{L}^{1,2}\,,\mathcal{L}^{2,1}\}
act within the vacuum
v_{1}
.
The fusion rules of these lines can be determined to be

\begin{split}\mathcal{L}^{1,1}\mathcal{L}^{1,1}&=\mathcal{L}^{2,2}\,,\\
\mathcal{L}^{2,2}\mathcal{L}^{1,1}&=D_{1}^{\omega^{p-p^{\prime}}}\\
\mathcal{L}^{1,2}\mathcal{L}^{1,2}&=D_{1}^{\omega^{-p^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{2,1}\,,\\
\mathcal{L}^{2,1}\mathcal{L}^{1,2}&=D_{1}^{\omega^{p-p^{\prime}}}\,.\\
\end{split}

(3.103)

These lines are charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry such that the line
\mathcal{L}^{i,j}
has a braiding phase of
\omega^{in}
with
D_{1}^{\omega^{n}}
.
Finally, there F-symbols incur contributions form both the symmetry and physical boundaries that are labeled by
p
and
p^{\prime}
in
H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},U(1))
respectively.
Concretely these are

F(\mathcal{L}^{i,i^{\prime}}\,,\mathcal{L}^{j,j^{\prime}}\,,\mathcal{L}^{k,k^{\prime}})=\exp\left\{\frac{2\pi ip}{9}i(j+k-[j+k]_{3})-\frac{2\pi ip^{\prime}}{9}i^{\prime}(j^{\prime}+k^{\prime}-[j^{\prime}+k^{\prime}]_{3})\right\}\,.

(3.104)

As this phase has 2 vacua exchanged by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
and topological lines charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry, it is the phase where the full 2-group symmetry is spontaneously broken.
The symmetry breaking pattern of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry is labeled by
p-p^{\prime}\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},U(1))
and the underlying TFT realizing this phase is a 2-group SSB phase:

2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
2-Group SSB Phase

3.4.3
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
SPT Phase

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),t}\,.

(3.106)

The order parameters are given by the defects that can end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
.
These are the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
and the surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
.
The line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
does not end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
, therefore after compactifying the SymTFT, one obtains a single topological local operator, which is the identity.
Correspondingly, there is a single vacuum on which the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{0}
acts trivially.
The
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line has two ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
which are uncharged and in the twisted sectors of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
generators.

(3.107)

The resulting gapped phase is therefore trivial from the point of view of 1-form symmetry.
The
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
surface ends on a single untwisted line
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{b}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
which has F-symbols given by
t
.
On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
ends on the line
(D_{2}^{b}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[b]})
.
After compactifying the SymTFT, one obtains a line in the
D_{2}^{b}
twisted sector with F-symbols given by
t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
:

(3.111)

We denote the two genuine lines obtained after compactifying the SymTFT with
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
stretched between both ends as
\mathcal{L}^{j}
.
Using compatibility between bulk fusions of
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
and fusion of the ends
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{j}}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[a]}
.
It follows that
\mathcal{L}^{j}
have the fusion rules of flux lines in
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
DW theory with the topological action given by
p-p^{\prime}\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},U(1))
.
These ends braid with the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
1-form generators on the symmetry boundary and therefore correspond to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
SSB phase.
Finally the surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
has a single untwisted end
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[b]}
on the physical boundary and a single twisted end
(D_{2}^{b}/\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}},\mathcal{E}^{[b]}_{1})
on the symmetry boundary.
Therefore the generalized charge corresponding to
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
is in the
D_{2}^{b}
twisted sector implying that the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry is spontaneously preserved in this phase.

To summarize, this gapped phase corresponds to a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
SSB phase and is realized by a 3d DW theory with a 3-cocycle twist determined by
p
and
p^{\prime}
.

2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}

(3.112)

3.5
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
Gapped Phases

We now consider the symmetry boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),t}\,,

(3.113)

which carries the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
symmetry on it, which is a non-invertible symmetry of 2-representations of the 2-group.

3.5.1
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB Phase

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\,.

(3.114)

The order parameters carry the generalized charges
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
as these are the bulk lines that have untwisted ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
.
First, let us consider the bulk line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
.
This has two untwisted sector ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
denoted as
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,1}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,2}
.
On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
has one untwisted end

{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}={\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,1}+{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,2}
and one
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
twisted end
{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,-}={\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,1}-{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,2}
.
Compactifying the SymTFT, one obtains a three dimensional space of untwisted local operators spanned by

\left\{1\,,\mathcal{O}^{1}\,,\mathcal{O}^{2}\right\}\,,

(3.115)

where
\mathcal{O}^{i}
denotes the local operator obtained by compactifying
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
with the ends
{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,i}
on the symmetry and physical boundary respectively.

(3.116)

This SymTFT sandwich is denoted as

\mathcal{O}^{i}=({\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,i})\,.

(3.117)

The algebra of these operators can be obtained from the algebra of ends of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
.
Recall that these ends transformed as a doublet under the
S_{3}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
Then by using the intertwiners of
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
, one obtains

\begin{split}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}&=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}\,,\\
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}&=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\,,\\
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}&=\lambda(1+\mathcal{E}_{0}^{P})\,,\\
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}&=\lambda(1-\mathcal{E}_{0}^{P})\,.\end{split}

(3.118)

with exactly the same relations for
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}^{E,i}_{0}
.
These rules imply that

\begin{split}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}&=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}+2\lambda\,,\\
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}&=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}-2\lambda\,,\\
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}&=-\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}+2\lambda\mathcal{E}_{0}^{P}\,,\\
\end{split}

(3.119)

Using these one can compute the OPE of operators local operators
\mathcal{O}^{1}
and
\mathcal{O}^{2}
as

\begin{split}\mathcal{O}^{1}\mathcal{O}^{1}&=({\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\otimes{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,1}\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,1})\\
&=({\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,2})\,,\\
&=\mathcal{O}^{2}\,,\\
\mathcal{O}^{1}\mathcal{O}^{2}&=({\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\otimes{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,1}\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,2})\\
&=(2\lambda\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\text{id}}\,,\lambda)\\
&=2\lambda^{2}\,.\end{split}

(3.120)

We choose the normalization
\lambda=1/\sqrt{2}
, such that the fusion rules take the convenient form
Similarly, we get

\mathcal{O}^{1}\mathcal{O}^{2}=\mathcal{O}^{2}\mathcal{O}^{1}=1\,,\qquad\mathcal{O}^{1}\mathcal{O}^{1}=\mathcal{O}^{2}\,,\qquad\mathcal{O}^{2}\mathcal{O}^{2}=\mathcal{O}^{1}\,.

(3.121)

These are
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
fusion rules and the idempotents (vacua) are constructed by a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
fourier transform as

v_{j}=\frac{1+\omega^{j}\mathcal{O}^{1}+\omega^{2j}\mathcal{O}^{2}}{3}\,.

(3.122)

To compute the action of the non-invertible symmetry
D_{2}^{A}
on these vacua, we recall that
D_{2}^{A}
descends from
D_{2}^{a}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{2}}
on upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
.
The sphere linking action of
D_{2}^{a}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{2}}
on
\mathcal{E}^{E,j}
is given by
\omega^{j}+\omega^{2j}=-1
.
Therefore we have

D_{2}^{A}:(1,\mathcal{O}^{1}\,,\mathcal{O}^{2})\longmapsto(2,-\mathcal{O}^{1}\,,-\mathcal{O}^{2})\,.

(3.123)

The action on the vacua can be immediately read off

D_{2}^{A}:(v_{0}\,,v_{1}\,,v_{2})\longmapsto(v_{1}+v_{2}\,,v_{2}+v_{0}\,,v_{0}+v_{1})\,.

(3.124)

This is rather unsurprising as this is essentially the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{a}
broken phase where
D_{2}^{A}
is realized as
D_{2}^{a}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{2}}
.
Next we move on to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry generated by
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
.
There are three
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
twisted order parameters in this gapped phase.
These are

\begin{split}(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\mathcal{O}^{P})&=\left((D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{P})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{P}\right)\,,\\
(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\overline{\mathcal{O}}^{1})&=\left((D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,-})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}^{E,1}_{0}\right)\,,\\
(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\overline{\mathcal{O}}^{2})&=\left((D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,-})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}^{E,2}_{0}\right)\,.\end{split}

(3.125)

Using similar methods as above, the algebra of these operators can be computed and we can construct their linear combinations that act within the three vacua
v_{0}\,,v_{1}
and
v_{2}
and are mapped into each other approprately under the
D_{2}^{A}
action.
Since there is an end of
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
line in each vacuum, the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry acts trivially in this phase.

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB with Trivial
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
(Confining Phase)

(3.126)

The non-invertible 0-form symmetry is realized on the vacua as

D_{2}^{A}=1_{01}\oplus 1_{02}\oplus 1_{12}\oplus 1_{10}\oplus 1_{21}\oplus 1_{20}\,.

(3.127)

3.5.2
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SPT Phase

Let us consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}),p}\,.

(3.128)

The order parameters correspond to the generalized charges
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
.
Firstly there in no bulk SymTFT line that ends on an untwisted operator on both boundaries.
Therefore after compactifying the SymTFT, one obtains a unique topological operator which is the identity.
Correspondingly, this phase has a unique vacuum.
Next, compactifying the SymTFT with the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
between both boundaries produces a local operator attached to the
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
line.

(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\mathcal{O}^{P})=\left((D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{P})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{P}\right)\,.

(3.129)

3.5.3
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB Phase

We now consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})\,,t}\,.

(3.135)

In this case, the bulk SymTFT defects
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
play the role of order parameters.
Let us first compute the vacua in this phase.
The SymTFT configuration with the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line extending between the two boundaries produces a unique local operator after compactification, since this line has a unique untwisted end on each boundary.

(3.136)

We denote this operator as
\mathcal{O}
and concretely, it is obtained as

\mathcal{O}=\left(\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}\right)\,.

(3.137)

Recall from (
3.119
) that
(\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+})^{2}=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}+\sqrt{2}
(we again fix
\lambda=1/\sqrt{2}
).
Then the OPE of the
\mathcal{O}
operator is

\begin{split}\mathcal{O}^{2}&=({\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\otimes{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+})\\
&=({\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+})+2({\mathcal{E}}_{\text{id}}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\text{id}}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{\text{id}})\,,\\
&=\mathcal{O}+2\,.\end{split}

(3.138)

Using the OPE of local operators, the idempotent operators are determined to be

v_{0}=\frac{2-\mathcal{O}}{3}\,,\qquad v_{1}=\frac{1+\mathcal{O}}{3}\,.

(3.139)

The
D_{2}^{A}
symmetry action can be computed using the fact that the sphere linking of
D_{2}^{A}
is

D_{2}^{A}:(1,\mathcal{O})\longmapsto(2,-\mathcal{O})\,,

(3.140)

which implies that the action on the vacua is

D_{2}^{A}:(v_{0}\,,v_{1})\longmapsto(v_{0}+2v_{1}\,,v_{0})\,.

(3.141)

In addition to the topological local operator
\mathcal{O}
, compactifying the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
also furnishes an operator
\overline{\mathcal{O}}
in the
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
twisted sector

(3.142)

denoted as

(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\overline{\mathcal{O}})=\left((D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}^{E,+}_{0}\right)\,.

(3.143)

In fact,
\overline{\mathcal{O}}
is the only
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
-twisted operator in the IR TQFT describing this gapped phase.
The OPE between the twisted and untwisted sector local operators is determined to be

(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\overline{\mathcal{O}})\cdot\mathcal{O}=-(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\overline{\mathcal{O}})

(3.144)

where we have used the fact
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}=-\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}
.
Now, the fate of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry in the two vacua can be understood from

\begin{split}(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\overline{\mathcal{O}})\cdot v_{0}&=(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\overline{\mathcal{O}})\,,\\
(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\overline{\mathcal{O}})\cdot v_{1}&=0\,.\end{split}

(3.145)

Which implies that the 1-form symmetry generator is isomorphic to the identity in the vacua
v_{0}
, i.e.,
v_{0}
realizes a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
trivial state.
Meanwhile there is no way to make the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
line end on
v_{1}
.
This implies that the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry is spontaneously broken in
v_{1}
.

Let us now move onto the order parameters carrying the generalized charge
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
.
For the order parameters, we only consider the untwisted sector ends of SymTFT operators on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
.
Therefore we obtain two lines from
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
, one genuine line and one line in the
D_{2}^{A}
twisted sector via the following configurations

\begin{split}\mathcal{L}^{b}&=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\right)\,,\qquad(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{L}^{Ab})=\left((D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\right)\,.\end{split}

(3.146)

\lxSVG@closescope }{{{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@transformcm{1.0}{0.0}{0.0}{1.0}{364.59145pt}{42.60632pt}\lxSVG@begingroup@{transform=matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 504.49 58.95)} \pgfsys@hbox{59}\lxSVG@closescope }}}
\lxSVG@closescope }}}
\lxSVG@closescope
\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}\end{split}

(3.147)

The fusion rule
\mathcal{L}^{b}\otimes\mathcal{L}^{b}
follows from the fact that
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}=\mathcal{E}^{\text{id}}_{1}
as

\mathcal{L}^{b}\otimes\mathcal{L}^{b}=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\otimes{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{b}\otimes\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{b}\right)=D_{1}^{\text{id}}\,,\\

(3.148)

Next, to compute the fusion rules
\mathcal{L}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{L}^{Ab}
, we require
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}
.
Recall that
\mathcal{E}^{Ab}_{1}
descends from the direct sum of lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}b}
in the twisted sectors of
D_{2}^{ab}
and
D_{2}^{a^{b}}
respectively on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
The fusion of these lines is given by the group composition in
S_{3}
, i.e.

\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}b}\right)\otimes\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}b}\right)=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}b}\right)\oplus\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{ab}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}b}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}b}\right)\,.

(3.149)

The decomposable line in the first parenthesis on the right hand side becomes
\mathcal{E}^{Ab}
upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
.
Meanwhile the second parenthesis
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\text{id}}
such that the two lines in the direct sum are exchanged under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
.
Therefore the 2-dimensional space of endomorphsims of
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\text{id}}
decomposes into a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
even and a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
odd space.
As a result after gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, we find

\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,.

(3.150)

Similarly, one may compute the fusion rule
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}
. By lifting to the ungauged boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
and then subsequently gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, one finds

\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{A}\,.

(3.151)

We are now ready to compute the remaining fusions among
\mathcal{L}^{Ab}
and
\mathcal{L}^{b}

\begin{split}\mathcal{L}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{L}^{Ab}&=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\otimes{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{b}\otimes\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{b}\right)\\
&=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{\text{id}}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{\text{id}}\right)\\
&=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{\text{id}}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{\text{id}}\right)\\
&=D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\\
\mathcal{L}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{L}^{b}&=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\otimes{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{b}\otimes\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{b}\right)\\
&=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{A}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{\text{id}}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{\text{id}}\right)=0\,.\end{split}

(3.152)

The fact that
\mathcal{L}^{Ab}\otimes\mathcal{L}^{b}=0
indicates that these lines act within distinct vacua.
Since
\mathcal{L}^{Ab}
is a
D_{2}^{A}
twisted line and only the vacuum
v_{0}
is symmetric with respect to
D_{2}^{A}
(from (
3.141
)), it follows that
\mathcal{L}^{Ab}
acts within
v_{0}
.
Meanwhile since
\mathcal{L}^{b}
is the order parameter for
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB, it only acts within
v_{1}
where this symmetry is broken.
Finally the lines
\mathcal{L}^{b}
and
\mathcal{L}^{Ab}
inherit the F-symbols
t-t^{\prime}\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
.
The
D_{2}^{A}
symmetry in this phase is realized concretely as

D_{2}^{A}=1_{00}\oplus B_{01}\oplus\overline{B}_{10}\,,

(3.153)

where
1_{00}
is the identity surface within
v_{0}
,
B_{01}
is the interface between
{\rm Triv}_{0}
and
{\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})}_{t-t^{\prime}}
and
\overline{B}_{10}
is the converse interface.
As a consistency check, we compute the fusion rules

\begin{split}D_{2}^{A}\otimes D_{2}^{A}&=\left(1_{00}\oplus B_{01}\oplus\overline{B}_{10}\right)\otimes\left(1_{00}\oplus B_{01}\oplus\overline{B}_{10}\right)\\
&=\left(1_{00}\oplus B_{01}\oplus\overline{B}_{10}\right)\oplus(B\overline{B})_{00}\oplus(\overline{B}B)_{11}\\
&=D_{2}^{A}\oplus\frac{D_{2}^{\text{id}}}{D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}}\,.\end{split}

(3.154)

Where in the line we have used the fact that
(B\overline{B})_{00}=1_{00}\oplus 1_{00}
, which is the condensation defect in
v_{0}
where
D_{1}^{\widehat{h}}\sim D_{1}^{\text{id}}
and
(\overline{B}B)_{11}
is indeed the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
condensation defect in
v_{1}
.

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB Phase (“Superstar”)

(3.155)

The non-invertible 0-form symmetry is realized on the vacua as

D_{2}^{A}=1_{00}\oplus B_{01}\oplus\overline{B}_{10}\,.

(3.156)

Note that this phase is very interesting – we will refer to it as the superstar phase. It has a confining 1-form symmetry in one vaccum, and a deconfined 1-form symmetry in the other, which is thus described by a DW theory. The symmetry acts non-trivially on these two vacua. This is the phase we referred to in the introduction as having two vacua, with different TQFTs in each. this is a new physical feature in this class of models. We will see similar phases for other
2\mathsf{Rep}(\mathbb{G}^{(2)})
symmetries.

3.5.4
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB Phase

Let us now consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3}),(p,t^{\prime})}\,.

(3.157)

The order parameters carry generalized charges
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
.
Since neither of these
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
symmetry mulitplets contain any local operators, there is only the single identity local operator in the IR TQFT describing this gapped phase.
Correspondingly this phase has a single vacuum
v_{0}=1
, on which the
D_{2}^{A}
symmetry acts as

D_{2}^{A}=\frac{D_{2}^{\text{id}}}{D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}}\,.

(3.158)

The SymTFT surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
provides a single line
\mathcal{L}^{A}
in the
D_{2}^{A}
twisted sector

(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{L}^{A})=\left((D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{A})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[a]}\right)\,.

(3.160)

To compute the fusion among
\mathcal{L}^{A}
, we need the fusions of the ends of
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
on the two boundaries.
These are

\begin{split}(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{A})\otimes(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{A})&=(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{A})\oplus\left(D_{2}^{C}\,,D_{1}^{C,\text{id}}\right)\,,\\
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}&=D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{P}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}\,.\end{split}

(3.161)

where we denote the
D_{2}^{C}:=D_{2}^{\text{id}}/\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
, with
\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}=D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
and the identity on the condensation surface as
D_{1}^{C,\text{id}}
.
Using these, the fusion rules of
\mathcal{L}^{A}
are determined to be

\begin{split}\mathcal{L}^{A}\otimes\mathcal{L}^{A}&=D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\oplus\mathcal{L}^{A}\,.\end{split}

(3.162)

The F-symbols of the
\mathcal{L}^{A}
line are controlled by the data
(p,t^{\prime})\in H^{3}(S^{3},U(1))
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
and we leave their explicit computation for the future.
Next, compactifying the configuration with the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
stretched between
both boundaries, furnishes both twisted sector and untwisted sector lines which we denote as
\mathcal{L}^{b}
and
\mathcal{L}^{Ab}
.
Let us focus on the untwisted sector line

\mathcal{L}^{b}=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[b]}\right)\,,

(3.163)

(3.164)

To compute its fusion rules, we require the fusions of the ends which are

\begin{split}\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}&=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\text{id}}\,,\\
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[b]}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[b]}&=(D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{E})\otimes(D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]})\,,\\
\end{split}

(3.165)

Using these, the fusion rules are determined to be

\mathcal{L}^{b}\otimes\mathcal{L}^{b}=D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{C,\text{id}}\,.

(3.166)

In particular, these lines are charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry and their F-symbols rules are determined by
{[t-t^{\prime}]}\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,U(1))
.
Therefore this is the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry broken phase, realizing the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with 3-cocycle
t-t^{\prime}
.

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:

The non-invertible 0-form symmetry is realized on the vacua as

D_{2}^{A}=\frac{D_{2}^{\text{id}}}{D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}}\,.

(3.168)

3.6
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
Gapped Phases

We now describe the minimal gapped phases obtained by choosing the symmetry boundary as

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}\,,

(3.169)

i.e., we choose the boundary with trivial discrete torsion in
H^{3}(S_{3}\,,U(1))
.
In what follows, we allow there to be non-trivial torsion on the physical boundary and construct all minimal gapped phases in this manner.

3.6.1
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
Trivial Phase

Let us consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\,.

(3.170)

The order parameters carry the generalized charges
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
for
R\in\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
.
Specifically any line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
extending accross the SymTFT between the two boundaries, provides
{\rm dim}(R)

(3.171)

(D_{1}^{R}\,,\mathcal{O}^{R,i})=\left((D_{1}^{R}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R,i}\right)\,.

(3.172)

All these ends transform trivially under the
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
symmetry and therefore this corresponds to the single vacuum phase where the entire
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
acts trivially.
Specifically any representation
R
just acts as
{\text{dim}}(R)
copies of the identity line.

This phase has a non-invertible 1-form symmetry
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
which is preserved. The associated line operators (charges) are confined.

2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
: Trivial Phase with trivial
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
1-form symmetry (Confining Phase)

denoted by

(D_{1}^{P}\,,\mathcal{O}^{P})=\left((D_{1}^{P}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{P})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{P}\right)\,.

(3.177)

This implies that the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\subset\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
is preserved as
D_{1}^{P}
is isomorphic to the identity line in the IR TQFT
describing this gapped phase.
Since there are no non-identity lines that end on both the physical and symmetry boundary, we obtain a unique local operator after compactification and correspondingly, there is a unique vacuum in this phase.
Next, we consider the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
generalized charge.
The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
has two untwisted ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
, which we denote as
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{a}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{a^{2}}
.
There is a single end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
which is also untwisted. We denote this as
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}
.
Therefore we obtain two lines

\mathcal{L}^{[a],a^{j}}=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{a^{j}}\right)\,,

(3.178)

depicted as

(3.179)

This line actually splits as
\mathcal{L}^{[a],a^{j}}
can emit the
D_{1}^{P}
line which can itself end on
\mathcal{O}^{P}
.
By shrinking
\mathcal{O}^{P}
onto
\mathcal{L}^{[a],a^{j}}
, we obtain an additional local operator on
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}
, implying that this line must split.
Similarly, the symmetry operator line
D_{1}^{E}
splits since it can emit a
D_{1}^{P}
line.
We find that in this phase
D_{1}^{E}
acts as

D_{1}^{E}=D_{1}^{\omega}\oplus D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}\,.

(3.180)

To understand the structure of this gapped phase, we find it illustrative to ungauge the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
symmetry on the symmetry boundary.
We then obtain the SymTFT with
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}
which corresponds to
2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB phase.
Recall that this phase had two vacua
v_{0}
and
v_{1}
exchanged under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
and each vacuum realized a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with 3-cocycle
p\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},U(1))
.
Upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
, we obtain a single vacuum theory with the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
spontaneously preserved.
The single vacuum again realizes the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with 3-cocycle
p\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},U(1))
with the
D_{1}^{E}
symmetry realized as (
3.180
).
The gapped phase can be summarized as

2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})/2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
SSB Phase:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
preserved (Confining) and SSB for
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
1-form symmetry

(3.181)

The non-invertible 1-form symmetry is realized as

\begin{split}D_{1}^{P}\simeq D_{1}^{\text{id}}\,,\qquad D_{1}^{E}\simeq D_{1}^{\omega}\oplus D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}\,,\end{split}

(3.182)

i.e.,
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
acts on this gapped phase via the projection
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\to 2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
.

3.6.3
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
SSB Phase

Now we consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),t}\,.

(3.183)

The order parameters are provided by the generalized charges
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
.
The generalized charge
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
contributes a local operator in the twisted sector of
D_{1}^{E}
which is uncharged under the
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
symmetry

(D_{1}^{E}\,,\mathcal{O}^{E})=\left((D_{1}^{E}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}\right)\,.

(3.185)

Therefore in this phase the
D_{1}^{E}
line is isomorphic to the identity.
The
D_{1}^{P}
symmetry remains non-trivial as there is no
D_{1}^{P}
twisted sector in this phase.
By consistency with
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
fusion rules, it can be determined that
D_{1}^{E}
acts as

D_{1}^{E}=D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{P}\,,

(3.186)

in this phase.

generalized charge—this contributes a untwisted sector line operator

(3.188)

This line is charged under
D_{1}^{P}
and has
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
fusion rules with the F-symbols given by
t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,U(1))
.
Therefore we determine this phase to be the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with a 3-cocycle twist
t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
.
From the perspective of the
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
, this corresponds to the phase where the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
subsymmetry is spontaneously broken as the IR TQFT contains the line
\mathcal{L}^{b}
charged under it.

2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})

(3.189)

The
D_{1}^{P}
1-form symmetry is generated by the topological charge line of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory while the
D_{1}^{E}
symmetry is generated by

\begin{split}D_{1}^{E}\simeq D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{P}\,.\end{split}

(3.190)

In summary,
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
acts on this gapped phase via the projection
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\to 2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
.
Only the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
acts faithfully within this phase and is spontaneously broken.

3.6.4
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
SSB Phase

Finally we consider the case where the physical boundary is

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})\,,(p,t)}\,.

(3.191)

In this case the order parameters are the generalized charges
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
.
Each of these charges provide a single untwisted line charged under the
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
symmetry as

\begin{split}\mathcal{L}^{[a]}&=(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[a]})\,,\\
\mathcal{L}^{[b]}&=(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[b]}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[b]})\,,\end{split}

\mathcal{L}^{[b]}
which carry charges under
D_{1}^{E}
and
D_{1}^{P}
respectively, the full
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
symmetry is spontaneously broken in this phase.
There is a unique vacuum since the IR TQFT contains only a single topological local operator which is the identity.
Finally the F-symbols of the charged lines
\mathcal{L}^{[a]}
and
\mathcal{L}^{[b]}
are controlled by the 3-cocycle
(p,t)\in H^{3}(S_{3},U(1))
.
This gapped phase is the
S_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with a
(p,t)
3-cocycle twist.

2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
SSB

\begin{split}\hbox to58.28pt{\vbox to17.72pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 29.14078pt\lower-8.86078pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke=#000000} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill=#000000} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width=0.4pt} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} {{}}{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}
{{}}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\hbox{\hbox{{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} {{}{}{{
{}{}}}{
{}{}}
{{}{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}}{{}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}{}{{}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces
}{{{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@transformcm{1.0}{0.0}{0.0}{1.0}{-25.80777pt}{-1.97223pt}\lxSVG@begingroup@{transform=matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -35.71 -2.73)} \pgfsys@hbox{59}\lxSVG@closescope }}}
\lxSVG@closescope }}}
\lxSVG@closescope
\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}\end{split}

(3.194)

The
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
1-form symmetry is generated by the Wilson lines of the
S_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory.
Since the IR theory contains topological lines charged under the full symmetry category, this is the
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
SSB phase.

3.7
Non-Minimal Gapped Boundary Conditions

We now describe non-minimal gapped boundary conditions for the
4d

S_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten.
The defining feature of such a boundary condition is that it contains non-trivial topological line defects that are not boundary projections of bulk line defects.
We follow the general strategy developed in
[
1
]
and outlined in Sec.
2
.

3.7.1
Non-minimal Dirichlet boundary condition

Clearly a simple class of boundary conditions is obtained by stacking the Dirichlet boundary condition by a 3d topological order.
Such boundaries are classified by a modular tensor categories (MTCs).
Given an MTC
\mathcal{M}
, which describes the topological line defects of a 3d TFT
\mathfrak{T}
, one can stack the Dirichlet boundary condition with
\mathfrak{T}
to obtain a new topological boundary

\mathfrak{B}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{\text{Dir}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}\,.

(3.195)

The 2-fusion category of topological defects on this boundary are

\mathcal{S}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}}\boxtimes\Sigma\mathcal{M}\,,

(3.196)

where
\Sigma\mathcal{M}
(sometimes also denotes as
{\rm Mod}(\mathcal{M})
) is the 2-category obtained by including all condensation defects constructible from the lines in
\mathcal{M}
, i.e., the Karoubi completion of
\mathcal{M}
into a 2-category.

In relation to bulk SymTFT defects, this boundary condition looks almost like
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, except that the bulk identity surface ends on
\mathfrak{B}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{\text{Dir}}
not only on the identity line but on any line in
\mathcal{M}
.
Likewise any other line or surface defect on the boundary can be stacked with an object in
\Sigma\mathcal{M}
without affecting its bulk lift.

3.7.2
Non-minimal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
Neumann boundary condition

We now describe the non-minimal generalization of the
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}
boundary condition.
We will restrict ourselves to the simpler case where there is no discrete torsion while gauging.
Such a boundary condition is defined by stacking
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
with a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(0)}
symmetric 3d TFT
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
whose lines defects form the modular tensor category
\mathcal{M}
.
Given
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
, we define the non-minimal generalization of the
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}
boundary condition as

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}^{\mathfrak{T}}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(0)}}\,.

(3.197)

The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetry is defined via a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
-crossed braided extension of
\mathcal{M}
, denoted as

\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}=\bigoplus_{g\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}\mathcal{M}^{g}\,.

(3.198)

Here
\mathcal{M}^{g}
denotes the category of lines living at the end of the
g
condensation defect.
From
\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
, there is a well defined construction known as equivariantization
[
64
,
5
]
to gauge the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetry to obtain a larger MTC
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}
.
The lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}
have a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
grading

\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}=\bigoplus_{g\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{g}\,,\qquad\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{g}=\mathcal{M}^{g}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\,.

(3.199)

Among these the lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
are unattached to any bulk surface.
In particular
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
contains lines
D_{1}^{\omega}
and
D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}
that generate the dual
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
symmetry and are obtainable from the boundary projection of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
.

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\Bigg|_{\mathfrak{B}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}}=\left\{(D_{1}^{\omega}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1})\,,(D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2})\right\}\,.

(3.200)

The rest of the lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
are intrinsic to the boundary.
The Müger center of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
is
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
generated by
D_{1}^{\omega}
, therefore these remaining lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
are all remotely detectable.
The bulk line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
continues to end on a local operator that is charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\Bigg|_{\mathfrak{B}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}}=\left\{\mathcal{O}^{P}\right\}\,.

(3.201)

The lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a^{2}}
descend from the
a
and
a^{2}
twisted sectors, i.e.,
\mathcal{M}^{a}
and
\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}
and become attached to the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
.

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}\Bigg|_{\mathfrak{B}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}}=\left\{\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a^{2}}\right\}\,.

(3.202)

The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
has a single end (upto fusion with genuine lines) in the twisted sector of
D_{2}^{b}/\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\Bigg|_{\mathfrak{B}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}}=\left\{(D_{2}^{b}/\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b})\right\}

(3.203)

The remaining lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1}
appear simply at the end of the identity surface and are unattached to any bulk defect in the SymTFT.
Note that the fusion 2-category of genuine topological defects on this boundary is

\Sigma\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1}\,.

(3.204)

3.7.3
Non-minimal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Neumann boundary condition

To construct non-minimal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Neumann boundary conditions, we follow the same approach as before.
First we stack the Dirichlet boundary condition with a 3d TFT whose underlying modular category of lines
\mathcal{M}
can be enriched by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
to obtain the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
crossed braided extension of
\mathcal{M}
denoted as

\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}=\mathcal{M}^{1}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{p}\,.

(3.205)

Here the category of lines
\mathcal{M}^{1}\equiv\mathcal{M}
while the lines in the non-trivial grade
\mathcal{M}^{p}
appear at the end of a condensation defect (say
D_{2}^{\phi}
) with
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
fusion rules.
We then gauge the diagonal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
generated by
D_{2}^{b}\otimes D_{2}^{\phi}
.
We denote the gapped boundary condition thus obtained as

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})}^{\mathfrak{T}}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\rm diag}}\,.

(3.206)

Let us describe the end of the different bulk SymTFT defects after such a gauging.
Firstly, since the end
\mathcal{O}^{P}
of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
is charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry being gauged, this end goes to the twisted sector, i.e., it is attached to the
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
symmetry defect
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
.
Similarly, the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
also has the same ends as on the minimal boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})}
.
Apart from
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
, there are additional non-trivial lines on the boundary that come from the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
equivariantization of
\mathcal{M}^{1}
.
These lines (including
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
) form the braided fusion category

\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}\,,

(3.207)

whose Müger center is
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
generated by
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
.
Moving on to the bulk surfaces in the SymTFT—recall that on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
has two twisted sector ends
(D_{2}^{a},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a})
and
(D_{2}^{a^{2}},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}})
which are swapped by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
.
Im the minimal case, these twisted sector lines combined into a single line upon
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
gauging.
In the process of non-minimal gauging, one may further stack
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a}
and
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}}
with any line
D_{1}^{x}
in
\mathcal{M}
and its partner
D_{1}^{\phi(x)}
under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
action respectively, and then gauge.
Doing so, one obtains a non-minimal end of
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
in the
D_{2}^{A}
twisted sector which we denote as
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ax}
.

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}=\left\{(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}^{Ax}_{1})\quad\Big|\quad x\in\mathcal{M}^{1}\right\}\,.

(3.208)

Finally, let us consider the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
.
On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, it had three ends.
The end
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}
in the
D_{2}^{b}
twisted sector, now goes to the charged sector of the dual 1-form symmetry generated by
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
.
Additionally any line in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{p}=\mathcal{M}^{p}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
carries a charge under
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
and become attached to
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
.
Furthermore, the ends
(D_{2}^{ab}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{ab})
and
(D_{2}^{a^{2}b}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}b})
were exchanged under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
and have a similar fate as the ends of the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
described above.
Following the same logic, we obtain,

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}=\left\{D_{1}^{x}\,,(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Aby})\quad\Big|\quad x\in\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{p}\,,y\in\mathcal{M}\right\}\,,

(3.209)

Here
(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Aby})
denotes the image of the following
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
invariant defect under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
gauging

(D_{2}^{a}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{ab}\otimes D_{1}^{y})\otimes(D_{2}^{a}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}b}\otimes D_{1}^{\phi(y)})\xrightarrow{{\rm gauging}\ {\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}}(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Aby})\,.

(3.210)

3.7.4
Non-minimal
S_{3}
Neumann boundary condition

The non-minimal generalization of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}
is defined as

\mathfrak{B}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}}{S^{\rm diag}_{3}}\,,

(3.211)

where
\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}
is an
S_{3}
symmetric TFT whose underlying modular tensor category of lines is
\mathcal{M}
.
The
S_{3}
enrichment of
\mathfrak{T}
is defined via an
S_{3}
crossed braided fusion category

\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{S_{3}}=\bigoplus_{g\in S_{3}}\mathcal{M}^{g}\,.

(3.212)

Physically
\mathcal{M}^{g}
describes the lines at the end of the
g
symmetry condensation defect.
Let us now describe the gauging of
S_{3}
within the SymTFT setup.
On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}
, the SymTFT line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
, ended on a multiplet of local operators
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R,i}
, transforming in the
R
representation of
S_{3}
.
Upon gauging
S_{3}
, this multiplet combines into a single operator attached to the
D_{1}^{R}
symmetry defect

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}\Bigg|_{\mathfrak{B}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}}=(D_{1}^{R}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R})\,.

(3.213)

Next, on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}
the surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}
ended on lines in
\mathcal{M}^{1}
.
Gauging
S_{3}
, one obtains lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}\equiv\mathcal{M}^{1}/S_{3}
.
Concretely, the lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
descend from indecomposable orbits under the
S_{3}
action in
\mathcal{M}^{1}
.
Furthermore if a representative line in an
S_{3}
orbit is stabilized by (i.e. is invariant under)
H\subseteq S_{3}
, then it can further carry a representation
R_{H}\in\mathsf{Rep}(H)
.

Similarly, the lines in
\mathcal{M}^{a}
and
\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}
were in the twisted sector of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
subgroup of the
S_{3}
diagonal symmetry being gauged to get from
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}
to
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}^{\mathfrak{T}}
.
Therefore these lines become untwisted sector lines that are charged under the dual
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
symmetry.
Furthermore since any given line in
\mathcal{M}^{a}
is mapped to another line in
\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}
under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry in
S_{3}
, such pairs of lines become simple (indecomposable) lines on the gauged boundary.
These lines are objects in

\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[a]}\equiv[\mathcal{M}^{a}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}]/S_{3}\,,

(3.214)

and are attached to
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
in the bulk. We denote this as

Q_{2}^{[a]}\Bigg|_{\mathfrak{B}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}}=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[a]}\,.

(3.215)

For precisely the same reason, one obtains lines in

Q_{2}^{[b]}\Bigg|_{\mathfrak{B}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}}=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[b]}\,,\qquad\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[b]}\equiv[\mathcal{M}^{b}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}b}]/S_{3}\,.

(3.216)

3.8
Non-Minimal Gapped Phases for Minimal Symmetries

We now discuss the gapped phases obtained by picking the physical boundary to be non-minimal and the symmetry boundary to be a minimal boundary.
For simplicity, we do not consider any discrete torsion on either physical or symmetry boundary.

3.8.1
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}^{\mathfrak{T}}

Since the physical boundary is obtained by simply stacking the minimal Dirichlet boundary with a 3d TFT
\mathfrak{T}
whose underlying MTC of lines is
\mathcal{M}
, the corresponding gapped phase is also just the stacking of the minimal gapped phase with
\mathfrak{T}
.

Let the minimal gapped phase obtained from compactifying the SymTFT sandwich with some minimal symmetry boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and physical boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
be denoted as

\left(\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}\,,\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\right)=\mathfrak{T}_{\rm min}\,.

(3.217)

Then the non-minimal gapped phase with Dirichlet type non-minimal boundary is

\left(\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}\,,\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}^{\mathfrak{T}}\right)=\mathfrak{T}_{\rm min}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}\,,

(3.218)

where the minimal symmetry
\mathcal{S}
corresponding to
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
is realized on
\mathfrak{T}_{\rm min}
and trivially on
\mathfrak{T}
.
Here the UV symmetry category is
\mathcal{S}
.
The system flows in the IR to TFT/gapped phase which contains emergent symmetries which include the non-trivial lines in
\mathcal{M}
that are all trivial in terms of their
\mathcal{S}
symmetry properties.

3.8.2
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}^{\mathfrak{T}}

Now we consider the physical boundary as

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}^{\mathfrak{T}}\equiv\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(0)}}\,.

(3.219)

The order parameters for the gapped phase with the physical boundary carry the generalized charges
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}
since these can end in untwisted sectors on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
.
Now let us describe the gapped phase obtained from the SymTFT by choosing different possible minimal symmetry boundaries.

•

Dirichlet Symmetry Boundary:
Let us consider
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
which carries a
2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}}
symmetry.
Firstly,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
becomes a local operator
\mathcal{O}^{P}
, which is charged under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\subset S_{3}
, therefore the global symmetry in this phase is broken down to
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
.
There are two vacua

v_{0}=\frac{1+\mathcal{O}^{P}}{2}\,,\qquad v_{1}=\frac{1-\mathcal{O}^{P}}{2}\,.

(3.220)

These are interchanged under
D_{2}^{b}
, while the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
generator
D_{2}^{a}
acts within each vacuum.
Next, the identity surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{\text{id}}
upon compactification provides lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
in each vacuum.
Crucially though, not all lines thus obtained in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
are independent.
Some of the lines are identified and some simple lines may split.
The reason for this is that there is a
\mathsf{Rep}(Z_{3})
category of lines (denoted
D_{1}^{\omega}
and
D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}
) on this boundary that are obtained from the projection of the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line onto the physical boundary.
Since the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line is trivialized on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
, the
\mathsf{Rep}(Z_{3})
lines in this gapped phase can actually end.
As a consequence any two lines
D_{1}^{x}
and
D_{1}^{y}
in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
that are related by the
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
action,

{\rm Hom}_{\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}}\left(D_{1}^{x}\otimes D_{1}^{\omega}\,,D_{1}^{y}\right)\neq 0\,,

(3.221)

are identified. Furthermore any simple line in
D_{1}^{x}
in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
that satisfies

{\rm Hom}_{\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}}\left(D_{1}^{x}\,,D_{1}^{x}\otimes(D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\omega}\oplus D_{1}^{\omega^{2}})\right)=\mathbb{C}^{N}\,,

(3.222)

splits into the direct sum of
N
simple lines.
This gives precisely the de-equivariantization of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
by
\mathsf{Rep}(Z_{3})
.
This is also referred to as gauging 1-form symmetry or anyon condensation
[
76
,
77
,
78
]
in various literature.
The de-equivariantization of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
gives back the MTC
\mathcal{M}
.
Therefore each vacuum realizes a
\mathfrak{T}
topological order described by
\mathfrak{T}=\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{C})
.
Lastly, the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
upon compactification provides two end within each vacuum that are attached to
D_{2}^{g}
for
g\in[a]
and carry a line in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{g}\in\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
.
For exactly the same reasons as described above,
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{g}\in\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
is de-equivariantized by
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
to give back
\mathcal{M}^{g}
.
In summary, we realize a two vacuum theory with each vacuum realizing a SET phase described by
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
, a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
crossed braided fusion category with underlying MTC
\mathcal{M}
.

2\mathsf{Vec}(S_{3})
:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
SSB
\boxtimes

{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
SET Phase

\begin{split}\hbox to196.04pt{\vbox to57.28pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 98.58551pt\lower-40.94865pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke=#000000} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill=#000000} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width=0.4pt} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} {{}}{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}

Neumann
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
Symmetry Boundary:
Take the symmetry boundary to be
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}
.
The corresponding gapped phase can be obtained by gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(0)}
symmetry in the phase (
3.223
).
Since the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetry acts within each vacuum.
We can just focus on the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
gauging of a single vacua realizing
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
.
This produces an theory
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
whose underlying MTC of lines is
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}
in (
3.199
).
Since the theory
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
contains lines that braid non-trivially with the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry generated by
D_{1}^{\omega}
, the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
1-form symmetry is spontaneously broken.
Both the vacua realize the same phase
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
and are exchanged by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
.
In summary, this gapped phase has the form

2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
: Non-minimal 2-group SSB

(3.224)

This phase can also be directly obtained from the SymTFT compactification.
Since
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
ends on both boundaries, it provides an additional topological local operator which is charged under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
and therefore there are two vacua exchanged by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
.
The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
can also end on both boundaries and provides lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a^{2}}
in each vacuum.
The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}
also ends on both boundaries and provides lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
in each vacuum.
Since
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
no longer ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
, we do not need to perform any 1-form gauging.

Neumann
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Symmetry Boundary:
We now take the symmetry boundary to be
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})}
.
The corresponding gapped phase can be obtained by gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry in the phase (
3.223
).
Since the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry acts exchanged the two vacua.
We obtain a theory with a single vacuum where the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry generated by
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
acts trivially.
The non-invertible symmetry
D_{2}^{A}
acts as
D_{2}^{a}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{2}}
.
Therefore we obtain the fusion rules

D_{2}^{A}\otimes D_{2}^{A}=D_{2}^{A}\oplus 2D_{2}^{\text{id}}\,,

(3.225)

which are consistent with
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
fusion rules.
In particular the surface
D_{2}^{A}
can end, i.e., it is isomorphic to the identity surface in this phase.
The lines that live at the end of the
D_{2}^{A}
surface are obtained from the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
quotient of
\mathcal{M}^{a}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}
.
Since these two grades of
\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
are exchanged by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
, elements in the quotient are simply order 2
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
orbits in
\mathcal{M}^{a}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}
.
To summarize, the underlying 3d TFT is

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
: Non-minimal
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SPT Phase

\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}\,,

(3.226)

described by the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
crossed braided fusion category
\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
.
On this the
2\mathsf{Rep}(\mathbb{G}^{(2)})
symmetry acts as
D_{2}^{A}\simeq D_{2}^{a}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{2}}
and
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\simeq D_{1}^{\text{id}}
.

We can also recover this phase directly from the SymTFT.
For this choice of symmetry boundary, both the order parameters i.e., are in twisted sectors.
Since
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
is in the twisted sector of
\mathsf{D}_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
, the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
sub-symmetry in
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
is trivial in this phase.
The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
after compactification, provide
D_{2}^{A}
twisted sector lines that are
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
invariant lines in
\mathcal{M}^{a}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}
.
Finally, the identity surface provides lines in
\mathcal{M}
that are uncharged under the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
symmetry.

Neumann
S_{3}
Symmetry Boundary:
We now take the symmetry boundary to be
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}
.
The corresponding gapped phase is obtained via a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
gauging of (
3.224
).
The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry was spontaneously broken in the gapped phase (
3.224
).
An equivalent statement is that the IR TFT describing this phase has a topological local operator
\mathcal{O}^{P}
charged under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
.
Upon gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry
\mathcal{O}^{P}
becomes a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
twisted sector operator and therefore the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
is realized trivially in this phase.
Furthermore, this phase has a single (identity) local operator and correspondingly a unique vacuum which realizes the 3d TFT
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
.
The structure of this gapped phase can be be summarized as

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
: Non-minimal
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})/2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
SSB Phase

The underlying 3d TFT is

\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}\,,

(3.227)

described by the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
crossed braided fusion category
\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
.
On this the
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
symmetry acts via its projection to
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
.
Specifically, the
D_{1}^{E}
symmetry on this phase is realized via
D_{1}^{\omega}\oplus D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}
.

3.8.3
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})}^{\mathfrak{T}}

We now consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})}^{\mathfrak{T}}\equiv\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}\,.

(3.228)

The order parameters for the gapped phase with the physical boundary carry the generalized charges
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}
since these can end in untwisted sectors on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
.
Let us describe the gapped phases obtained from the SymTFT sandwich with
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
being different possible minimal gapped boundaries.

•

Dirichlet Symmetry Boundary:
Let us pick

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\,.

(3.229)

In addition to the identity operator, there are two more local operators coming from compactifying the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line with the
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,i}
end on the symmetry boundary and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}
on the physical boundary.
These operators satisfy the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
algebra which was deduced in (
3.72
).
Correspondingly, there are 3 vacua given by (
3.73
).
The generators of the
S_{3}
0-form symmetry acts on these vacua as

\begin{split}D_{a}&:(v_{0}\,,v_{1}\,,v_{2})\longmapsto(v_{1}\,,v_{2}\,,v_{0})\,,\\
D_{b}&:(v_{0}\,,v_{1}\,,v_{2})\longmapsto(v_{0}\,,v_{2}\,,v_{1})\,,\\
\end{split}

(3.230)

Therefore none of the vacua are invariant under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetry, while
v_{j}
is invariant under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
generated by
D_{2}^{a^{j}b}
.
The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}
compactified between the physical and symmetry boundary provide the category of lines
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1}
.
The Müger center of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1}
is
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
generated by the projection of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
onto the physical boundary.
Now since
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
can end on the symmetry boundary, this
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
subcategory of lines is trivialized in this phase.
Equivalently, these anyon lines are condensed or equivalently, the lines at the end of
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}
are given by the de-equivariantization of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
which gives
\mathcal{M}^{1}
.
Similarly, the surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
has ends on the category of lines
\mathcal{M}^{p}
on the physical boundary.
Meanwhile on the symmetry boundary,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
has three ends denoted as
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{j}b}
in the twisted sector of
D_{2}^{a^{j}b}
respectively.
Since the vacuum
v_{j}
is invariant under
D_{2}^{a^{j}b}
, this topological surface can end within this vacuum and it does so on a line in
\mathcal{M}^{p}
.
In summary,

2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}}
:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
SSB
\boxtimes

{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
SET Phase

(3.231)

Each vacuum preserves a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry and realizes a
Z_{2}
SET
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
for the preserved
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
.
The structure of
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
is described by a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
crossed braided fusion category
\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}=\mathcal{M}^{1}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{p}
.

•

Neumann
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
Symmetry Boundary:
Take the symmetry boundary to be
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}
.
The corresponding gapped phase can be obtained by gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(0)}
symmetry in the phase (
3.231
).
The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetry is completely broken in (
3.231
), i.e., there are local order parameter operators transforming in each representation of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
.
After gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetry, these operators become attached to the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
generators and therefore the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry is realized trivially on the 2-group symmetric phase thus obtained.
Meanwhile the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry is realized precisely how it was within each vacuum in (
3.231
).
Therefore we obtain the
2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
symmetric gapped phase

2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
: Non-minimal SPT Phase

The underlying 3d TFT is

\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\,.

(3.232)

The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form symmetry is preserved and realized via the the symmetry enrichment of the MTC
\mathcal{M}
.
The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry is realized trivially on this phase

D_{1}^{\omega}\simeq D_{1}^{\text{id}}\,.

(3.233)

•

Neumann
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Symmetry Boundary:
Take the symmetry boundary to be
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})}
.
The phase thus obtained is a non-minimal version of the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB phase.
This phase is obtained by gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
symmetry in (
3.231
).
Note that there is a single vacuum i.e.,
v_{0}
which is invariant under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, i.e., the
D_{2}^{b}
surface may end on this vacuum.
Upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
-twisted sector lines become lines that are charged under the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry.
Therefore
v_{0}
maps to a vacuum in the gauged theory where
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
is spontaneously broken.
The 3d TFT realized in this phase is
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
whose underlying category of lines of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{p}
.
Meanwhile
v_{1}
and
v_{2}
which were exchanged by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
combine to a single vacuum in which the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry is realized trivially.
This vacuum realizes the 3d TFT
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
.

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
: Non-minimal
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB Phase

The underlying 3d TFT is
