Neumann
S_{3}
Symmetry Boundary:

Now we consider the case with
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}
.
The corresponding gapped phase can be obtained by gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry in (
3.232
).
Clearly this is simply

\mathfrak{T}_{Z_{2}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,.

(3.235)

Since the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
1-form symmetry was realized trivially on (
3.232
), correspondingly
D_{1}^{E}\simeq D_{1}^{\omega}\oplus D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}
is realized trivially on this
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
symmetric phase.
Meanwhile the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry was preserved in (
3.232
), which in fact realized a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
SET.
Therefore the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry is spontaneously broken in
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
.

2\mathsf{Rep}(\mathsf{S}_{3})
: Non-minimal
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
SSB Phase

The underlying 3d TFT is

\mathfrak{T}_{Z_{2}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,.

(3.236)

The non-invertible 1-form symmetry is realized trivially
D_{1}^{E}\simeq D_{1}^{\text{id}}
, while the
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
1-form symmetry is realized via the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Wilson line in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}=\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
.
This is a non-minimal deconfined phase for the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
symmetry.

3.8.4
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}^{\mathfrak{T}}

We now consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}^{\mathfrak{T}}\equiv\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}}{S_{3}}\,.

(3.237)

The order parameters for the gapped phase with the physical boundary carry the generalized charges
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
since these surfaces can end in untwisted sectors on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
.
Let us describe the gapped phases obtained from the SymTFT sandwich with
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
being different possible minimal gapped boundaries.

•

Dirichlet Symmetry Boundary:

We take
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
to be the minimal boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
which carries the
2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}}
symmetry.
The
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
lines end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
while they become non-trivial
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
lines on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
.
Recall that the lines on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}^{\mathfrak{T}}
form

\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}=\mathcal{M}^{[\text{id}]}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[a]}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[b]}\,,

(3.238)

with
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[g]}
attached to the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}
.
Within
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}
, there is a
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
fusion sub-category of lines generated by the boundary projections of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
.
From the above, it is clear that the
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
subcategory of lines is trivialized after compactifying the SymTFT.
Therefore we obtain the de-equivariantized braided fusion category with respect to
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}
which is

\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{S_{3}}=\bigoplus_{g\in S^{3}}\mathcal{M}^{g}\,.

(3.239)

Specifically the surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
has two twisted sector ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
which are
(D_{2}^{a}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a})
and
(D_{2}^{a^{2}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}})
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[a]}
worth of ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
.
As described above, upon compactifying the SymTFT with
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
extended between both boundaries, we obtain the de-equivariantization by
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\subset\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}
and therefore one obtains

(D_{2}^{a}\,,\mathcal{M}^{a})\quad\text{and}\quad(D_{2}^{a^{2}}\,,\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}})\,.

(3.240)

For precisely the same reason, upon compactifying the SymTFT with the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
surface stretched between the two boundaries, we obtain

(D_{2}^{b}\,,\mathcal{M}^{b})\,,\quad(D_{2}^{ab}\,,\mathcal{M}^{ab})\,,\quad(D_{2}^{a^{2}b}\,,\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}b})\,.

(3.241)

In summary

2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}}
:
S_{3}
SET Phase

The underlying 3d TFT is

\mathfrak{T}\,.

(3.242)

As an
S_{3}
symmetric theory, it is recognized to be
\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}
which is an
S_{3}
SET whose underlying
S_{3}
crossed braided fusion category is
\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{S_{3}}
.

•

Neumann
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
Symmetry Boundary:
Consider the case
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})}
which carries a 2-group symmetry.
With
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}^{\mathfrak{T}}
, this phase is directly obtained via the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
gauging of
\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}
whose underlying
S_{3}
-crossed braided fusion category is
\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{S_{3}}
.
We denote the phase thus obtained as

\frac{\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}\,.

(3.243)

Let us describe this phase from the SymTFT sandwich.
The
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
line can end on the symmetry boundary, and becomes the
D_{1}^{P}\in\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
line on the physical boundary.
The
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line has two twisted sector ends
(D_{1}^{\omega}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1})
and
(D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2})
, and becomes the
D_{1}^{E}\in\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
line on the physical boundary.
After compactifying the SymTFT,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
decomposes as
D_{1}^{\omega}\oplus D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}
which generate the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry.
On the physical boundary, the category of lines has the structure

\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}=\mathcal{M}^{[\text{id}]}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[a]}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[b]}\,,

(3.244)

where the fusion rules are compatible with products of conjugacy classes.
The lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[g]}
are attached to the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}
surface in the bulk.
Since the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
ends on a local operator on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
, after compactification, we obtain a de-equivariantization of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}
by
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})\subset\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
generated by
D_{1}^{P}
.
After such a de-equivariantization
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[g]}
become

\begin{split}\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}&\longmapsto\mathcal{M}^{1}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\,,\\
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[a]}&\longmapsto\mathcal{M}^{a}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\,,\\
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[b]}&\longmapsto(\mathcal{M}^{b}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}b})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\,.\end{split}

(3.245)

Now let us describe the different order parameters in this phase.
First, by considering the SymTFT configuration with
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
stretched between both boundaries, we obtain untwisted sector lines in

\mathcal{M}^{a}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\,,

(3.246)

that are charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
1-form symmetry. Therefore the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
1-form symmetry is spontaneously broken in this phase, whose spontaneous breaking is described by a 3d TFT whose underlying category of lines is

\mathcal{M}^{1}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\,.

(3.247)

Finally, by considering the SymTFT configuration with
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
stretched between both boundaries, we obtain
lines attached to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry defect

\left(D_{2}^{b}\,,(\mathcal{M}^{b}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}b})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\right)\,.

(3.248)

Thus this gapped phase corresponds to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
enrichment of a topological order that spontaneously breaks the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry.

2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Symmetry Enriched
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
SSB (deconfined) Phase

The underlying 3d TFT is

\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\,,

(3.249)

whose underlying category of lines is

\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}=\mathcal{M}^{1}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\,.

(3.250)

The lines in
\mathcal{M}^{a^{p}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
carry a charge
\omega^{p}
under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry, therefore this symmetry is spontaneously broken.
The vacuum preserves the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry whose twist defects carry lines

\left(\mathcal{M}^{b}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}b})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\right)\,.

(3.251)

This forms a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
crossed braided extension of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}
.

•

Neumann
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Symmetry Boundary:
Now let us consider the symmetry boundary to be
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})}
which carries the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
symmetry on it.
We obtain the gapped phase with
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}^{\mathfrak{T}}
by starting from the phase
\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}
(which was obtained with
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
as the symmetry boundary) and gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry.
Recall that
\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}
corresponded to an
S_{3}
crossed braided fusion category
\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{S_{3}}
.
Firstly it contains the geniune lines in
\mathcal{M}^{1}
.
Upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, we obtain the pre-modular tensor category of lines

\mathcal{M}^{1}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,

(3.252)

whose Müger center is given by the dual
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
to the 0-form
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry being gauged.
Moving on, note that the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
exchanged the grades

D_{2}^{b}:\mathcal{M}^{a}\longleftrightarrow\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}\,,\qquad D_{2}^{b}:D_{2}^{a}\longleftrightarrow D_{2}^{a^{2}}\,,

(3.253)

hence upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, we obtain topological lines in twisted sector of
D_{2}^{A}
.
In the pre-gauged theory, these lines come from the direct sum of a line in
\mathcal{M}^{a}
and its partner under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
action in
\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}
.
After gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, this becomes an indecomposable
D_{2}^{A}
twisted sector line.
Next, we consider the lines in
\mathcal{M}^{b}
attached to
D_{2}^{b}
surfaces in the pregauged theory.
Upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, these being untwisted sector lines

\mathcal{M}^{b}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,

(3.254)

charged under the dual
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
symmetry.
Finally since
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
also exchanged the grades

D_{2}^{b}:\mathcal{M}^{ab}\longleftrightarrow\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}b}\,,\qquad D_{2}^{b}:D_{2}^{ab}\longleftrightarrow D_{2}^{a^{2}b}\,,

(3.255)

upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, these become topological lines in twisted sector of
D_{2}^{A}
.

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
: Non-invertible symmetry enriched
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB (deconfined) Phase

This 3d phase corresponds to a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry broken phase whose lines form the MTC which has a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
graded structure

\mathcal{M}^{1}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{b}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,

(3.256)

where
\mathcal{M}^{b}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
are the lines that are charged under the 1-form symmetry.
The non-invertible 0-form symmetry acts as a condensation defect whose ends contain non-trivial lines in

(\mathcal{M}^{a}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\oplus(\mathcal{M}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{ab^{2}})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,.

(3.257)

•

Neumann
S_{3}
Symmetry Boundary:
We finally describe the gapped phase obtained by picking
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3})}
.
This phase is obtained by the
S_{3}
gauging of
\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}
.

2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
: Non-minimal
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
SSB (deconfined) Phase

The underlying 3d TFT is

\mathfrak{T}_{S_{3}}/S_{3}\,,

(3.258)

whose lines form the MTC

\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[a]}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[b]}\,,

(3.259)

graded by conjugacy classes in
S_{3}
.
The non-invertible 1-form symmetry is generated by the Müger center of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}

\mathcal{Z}_{2}(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]})=\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\,.

(3.260)

Since this MTC contains lines carrying under the lines the generate the 1-form
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
symmetry, it corresponds to the non-minimal
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
SSB phase.

4
Non-Invertible Symmetries and Phases from
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}})

The second class of examples that we will present in detail have as their SymTFT the
D_{8}
DW theory in 3+1d. This has several features that go beyond the ones observed in the
S_{3}
case, which will in fact also extend to
D_{2n}
, as will be discussed later.
For brevity (within the expanse of the present paper), we will focus on a discusion of the SymTFT, the minimal gapped BCs, and highlight the phases for the non-invertible 2-representation categories
2\mathsf{Rep}(\mathbb{G}^{(2)})
and
2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
.

4.1
SymTFT

The group of symmetries of a square,
D_{8}
, has various presentations. We will use the following:

\displaystyle D_{8}={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}=\big\langle r\,,\;x\ \big|\ r^{4}=x^{2}=\text{id}\,,\;xrx=r^{3}\,,\big\rangle\,.

(4.1)

The conjugacy classes
[g]
and their centralizer groups
H_{g}
are:

[g]

[\text{id}]

\left[r^{2}\right]

[r]=\left\{r,r^{3}\right\}

[x]=\left\{x,xr^{2}\right\}

[xr]=\left\{xr,xr^{3}\right\}

H_{g}

D_{8}

D_{8}

\mathbb{Z}_{4}^{r}

\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{x}\times\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{r^{2}}

\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{xr}\times\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{r^{2}}

(4.2)

Each conjugacy class labels a topological surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}
in the SymTFT:

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}\,.

(4.3)

The topological lines are the 1-endomorphisms of these surfaces and transform in the irreducible representations of the centralizers
H_{g}
of
g\in[g]
:

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}:

\displaystyle\text{1End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R};\ R=1,1_{r},1_{x},1_{xr},E\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})

(4.4)

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}:

\displaystyle\text{1End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[r^{2}],R};\ R=1,1_{r},1_{x},1_{xr},E\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}:

\displaystyle\text{1End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[xr],R};\ R=(\epsilon_{1},\epsilon_{2}),\;\epsilon_{i}=\pm\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}:

\displaystyle\text{1End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[x],R};\ R=(\epsilon_{1},\epsilon_{2}),\;\epsilon_{i}=\pm\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}:

\displaystyle\text{1End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[r],R};\ R=i^{p},\;p=0,1,2,3\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})\,.

In particular, the topological lines on the identity surface,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
, are labeled by irreducible representations of
D_{8}
, whose character table is:

\begin{array}[]{|c|ccccc|}\hline\cr&{[\text{id}]}&{\left[r^{2}\right]}&{[r]}&{[x]}&{[xr]}\\
\hline\cr 1&1&1&1&1&1\\
1_{r}&1&1&+1&-1&-1\\
1_{xr}&1&1&-1&-1&+1\\
1_{x}&1&1&-1&+1&-1\\
E&2&-2&0&0&0\\
\hline\cr\end{array}

Table 5:
D_{8}
character table

We denote by
1_{k}
for
k\in\{r,x,xr\}
a 1-dimensional irrep that is 1 on
[\text{id}],[r^{2}],[k]
and
-1
otherwise, whereas for the 2-dimensional
E
we chose the following matrix representation:

\mathcal{D}_{E}(r)=\begin{pmatrix}i&0\\
0&-i\end{pmatrix}\,,\qquad\mathcal{D}_{E}(x)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\
1&0\end{pmatrix}\,.

(4.5)

We start from the canonical Dirichlet boundary condition on which the topological defects form the 0-form symmetry
\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
and subsequently gauge various subcategories of defects on this
boundary to obtain the other minimal boundaries, which are summarized in table
6
.

4.2.1
Dirichlet Boundary Condition

2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
, is obtained by requiring all genuine bulk topological lines to end on local operators
\mathcal{E}^{R,i}

(4.6)

Specifically,

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{k}}\Bigg|_{{\text{Dir}}}=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{{1_{k}}}\,,\quad 1_{k}\in\{1,1_{r},1_{x},1_{xr}\}\,,\qquad{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\Bigg|_{{\text{Dir}}}=\left\{\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}\right\}\,.

(4.7)

Absence of non-genuine local operators and of condensation defects.

Since all topological lines end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, there are no non-genuine local operators nor condensation defects on this boundary. Indeed, we shall see that all surface operators, described in the next paragraph, are invertible and generate the
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
0-form symmetry group.

Surface operators.

All topological surface operators have Neumann boundary conditions: their projections onto the boundary become the symmetry generators
D_{2}^{g}
with linking action

D_{2}^{g}:\quad\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R,i}\longmapsto\sum_{j}\mathcal{D}_{R}(g)_{ij}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R,j}\,.

(4.8)

where
\mathcal{D}_{R}(g)
is the matrix representation of
g\in G
in the irrep
R
, since the local operators at the end of the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
SymTFT line transform in the
R
representation of
D_{8}
.
The 1d irreps coincide with their characters, listed in table
5
, whereas for the 2d irrep
E
we choose:

\mathcal{D}(r)=\begin{pmatrix}i&0\\
0&-i\end{pmatrix}\,,\qquad\mathcal{D}(x)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\
1&0\end{pmatrix}\,.

(4.9)

The fusion of surfaces follows the (invertible)
D_{8}
group multiplication rule:

D_{2}^{g}\otimes D_{2}^{h}=D_{2}^{gh}\,,\qquad g,h\in D_{8}\,.

(4.10)

L-shaped surface configurations.

The non-identity surfaces cannot end on the Dirichlet boundary, and form L-shaped configurations as in (
2.12
),

4.2.2
Neumann(
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
) Boundary Condition

Let us now gauge the normal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
subsymmetry of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
with discrete torsion

s\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,.

(4.14)

We denote

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}),s}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes{\rm SPT}_{s}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}\,.

(4.15)

After gauging, one obtains a dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
1-form symmetry and a residual 0-form symmetry

D_{8}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}=\{1\sim(1,r^{2}),\,x\sim(x,xr^{2}),\,r\sim(r,r^{3}),\,xr\sim(xr,xr^{3})\}\cong{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r}\,.

(4.16)

The symmetry on this boundary is therefore the 2-group

\mathcal{S}=2\mathsf{Vec}^{\omega}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{r}^{2}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),r}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x})

(4.17)

with a non-trivial anomaly

\displaystyle=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{2}}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{k}}\,,

(4.25)

where the charge of
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{k}}
under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),r}
0-form symmetry follows from the character table
5
.

Surfaces that cannot end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}),s}
.

On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, the surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}
was the non-simple combination
D_{2}^{r}\oplus D_{2}^{r^{3}}
, with a 2-dimensional space of topological local operators spanned by
D_{0}^{r},\,D_{0}^{r^{3}}
. These can be combined into local operators transforming under
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
:

D_{0}^{r,\pm}=D_{0}^{r}\pm D_{0}^{r^{3}}

(4.26)

of which
D_{0}^{r,-}
is charged under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),r^{2}}
. When gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),r^{2}}
, the SymTFT surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}
projects to a single surface on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}),s}
, that we denote as
D_{2}^{r}/\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}}
, on which
\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}}=D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
is condensed. Indeed, the
D_{0}^{r,-}
local operator, which was charged under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),r^{2}}
, becomes a twisted sector operator for
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{r}^{2}}
therefore the surface containing it can absorb the
D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
line. Such surface can also arise from the
L

2-group anomaly.

Let us recall the consequences of the 2-group anomaly
[
56
]

•

The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),r}
0-form symmetry is fractionalized on the line operator generating the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{r}^{2}}
1-form symmetry:

\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
D_{2}^{r}
D_{2}^{r}
=\quad\;\;-
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}

(4.32)

\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
D_{2}^{x}
D_{2}^{r}
=\;\;-
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
D_{2}^{x}
D_{2}^{r}

(4.33)

•

As discussed around eq. (
4.22
), the local operators
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}
(in the twisted sector for
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{r}^{2}}
) are fractionally charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),r}
generator
D_{2}^{r}
, transforming as
\pm i
respectively;

•

Additionally,
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r}
is fractionally charged under
D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
. This follows from the fact that
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r}\otimes\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r}=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{2}}
that has a braiding phase of
-1
with
D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
.

4.2.3
Neumann
({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r})
Boundary Condition

The boundary condition obtained by gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}
subsymmetry of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
with possible discrete torsion
p\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4},U(1))\cong{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
will be denoted by:

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes{\rm SPT}_{p}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}}\,.

(4.34)

After gauging one obtains a dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{\widehat{r}}
symmetry, and a residual 0-form symmetry given by:

D_{8}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}=\{1\sim(1,r,r^{2},r^{3}),\;x\sim(x,xr,xr^{2},x^{3})\}\cong{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}

(4.35)

that acts on the 1-form symmetry by exchanging
r\leftrightarrow r^{3}
, giving the 2-group symmetry
[
56
]

\mathcal{S}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}}\,.

(4.36)

Genuine local operator.

Since the operator
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{r}}
at the end of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{r}}
was untwisted and uncharged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}
symmetry, it remains unaltered after gauging

(4.37)

The local operator
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{{1_{r}}}
transforms with a
-1
under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
.

Lines generating the dual symmetry after gauging and condensation surfaces.

After gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(0),r}
symmetry of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, one obtains a dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1),\widehat{r}}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p}
, whose generator we denote by
D_{1}^{\widehat{r}}
. The algebras:

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}}

\displaystyle=D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}\,,

(4.38)

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{\widehat{r}}}

\displaystyle=D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{r}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{3}}\,,

(4.39)

can be condensed on the identity surface, giving rise to condensation defects

D_{2}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}}=\frac{D_{2}^{[\text{id}]}}{\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}}}\,,\qquad D_{2}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{\widehat{r}}}=\frac{D_{2}^{[\text{id}]}}{\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{\widehat{r}}}}\,.

(4.40)

Non-genuine local operators.

On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, the operators
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{x}}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{xr}}
transform as
-1
under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(0),r}
, therefore after gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}
, they become attached to the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{r}^{2}}\subset{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1),\widehat{r}}
symmetry generator
D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
.

(4.41)

Under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
, the local operator
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{x}}
is uncharged while
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1{xr}}
carries charge
-1
.

On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}},\;\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}
transform under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(0),r}
as
i
and
-i
respectively. Therefore, after gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}
, they become attached to the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}
symmetry generators
D_{1}^{\widehat{r}}
and
D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{3}}
respectively.

(4.42)

Furthermore, since
\mathcal{D}_{E}(x):\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\leftrightarrow\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, the corresponding twisted sector operators in
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p}
are also acted upon by the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
symmetry

D_{2}^{x}:\quad(D_{1}^{\widehat{r}},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1})\longleftrightarrow(D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{3}},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2})\,.

(4.43)

From which we read off the 2-group action of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
on
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1),r}

D_{2}^{x}:\quad D_{1}^{\widehat{r}}\longleftrightarrow D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{3}}\,.

(4.44)

twisted sector lines

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
become untwisted sector lines that are charged under the dual

symmetry on

(4.45)

The linking phase between
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{n}}
and
D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{m}}
is
i^{nm}
, while the F-symbols and fusion properties of
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{n}}
are controlled by the choice of
p\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
:

F(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{l}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{m}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{n}})=\exp\left\{\frac{2\pi ip}{16}\,l(m+n-[m+n]_{4})\right\}\,,

(4.46)

where
[m+n]_{4}\equiv m+n\text{ mod }4
.

Local operators on non-identity lines.

The 1d irrep
1_{r}
on
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[r^{2}]}
gives rise to a local operator
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{r}}
on
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{2}}
:

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[r^{2}],1_{r}}\Bigg|_{{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p}}

\displaystyle=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{2}}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{r}}\,,

(4.47)

charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
0-form symmetry.

Surfaces that cannot end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p}
.

When gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(0),r}
, the SymTFT surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}
becomes transparent. Since
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}
are related by fusing with
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}
, they must be identified on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p}
.
On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, the surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}
was the non-simple combination
D_{2}^{x}\oplus D_{2}^{xr}\oplus D_{2}^{xr^{2}}\oplus D_{2}^{xr^{3}}
, with a 4-dimensional space of topological local operators that can be combined into local operators transforming under
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})
:

D_{0}^{x,i^{n}}=D_{0}^{x}+i^{-n}D_{0}^{xr}+i^{-2n}D_{0}^{x}+i^{-3n}D_{0}^{xr^{3}}

(4.48)

with charge
i^{n}
under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(0),r}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
. When gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(0),r}
, the SymTFT surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}
projects to a single surface on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p}
, denoted as
D_{2}^{x}/\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{\widehat{r}}}
on which
\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{\widehat{r}}}
, eq. (
4.39
), is condensed.
D_{2}^{x}/\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{\widehat{r}}}
can also arise from the

(4.49)

D_{2}^{x}/\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{\widehat{r}}}
is in the same Schur component as the invertible surface
D_{2}^{x}
that generates the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
subsymmetry of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p}

[
56
]
.

4.2.4
Neumann
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}})
and Neumann
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{2}})
Boundary Conditions

The SymTFT boundary condition obtained by gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),{xr}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),xr^{3}}
subsymmetry of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
with possible discrete torsion

t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}

(4.50)

will be denoted as:

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes{\rm SPT}_{t}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\,.

(4.51)

where the gauged
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
is the diagonal of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}\subset D_{8}
and the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry of SPT
t
.
Since
D_{8}
can be presented equivalently as:

\displaystyle\mathbb{Z}_{4}^{r}\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{xr}:

\displaystyle\{\text{id},\,r,\,r^{2},\,r^{3},xr,xr^{2},xr^{3},x\}

(4.52)

\displaystyle\mathbb{Z}_{4}^{r}\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{x}:

\displaystyle\{\text{id},\,r,\,r^{2},\,r^{3},x,xr,xr^{2},xr^{3}\}

there is an outer automorphism that relates
x
and
xr
, so the features of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{2}},t)}
can be deduced from those of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}
by mapping from the first to the second presentation of
D_{8}
in equation (
4.52
).

After gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}
0-form symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, one obtains
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}
with a dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{xr}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{xr}^{3}}
1-form symmetry and a residual 0-form symmetry given by:

D_{8}/({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{2}})=\{1\sim(1,xr,r^{2},xr^{3}),\;x\sim(x,r,xr^{2},r^{3})\}\cong{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}

(4.53)

that acts on the 1-form symmetry by exchanging
xr\leftrightarrow xr^{3}
, giving the 2-group symmetry

\mathcal{S}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),xr^{3}})\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}}\,.

(4.55)

The local operator
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{{1_{xr}}}
transforms with a
-1
under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
.

Lines generating the dual symmetry after gauging and condensation surfaces.

After gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),xr^{3}}
symmetry of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, one obtains a dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{xr}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{xr}^{3}}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}
, whose generators we denote by
D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}}\,,\;D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}^{3}}
. The full list of condensation surfaces and their fusion is provided in sec. 5.7 of
[
56
]
.

Non-genuine local operators.

On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, the operators
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{x}}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{r}}
transform as
-1
under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),xr}
and
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),xr^{3}}
, therefore after gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),xr^{3}}
, they become attached to the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{xr}}
symmetry generator
D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}}
.

(4.56)

Under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
, the local operator
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{x}}
is uncharged while
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{r}}
carries charge
-1
. We can unitarily transform
\mathcal{D}_{E}(xr)=\sigma^{y}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\
i&0\end{pmatrix}
to
\sigma^{z}=\text{diag}(1,-1)
. Let us denote by

\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,\pm i}:=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\pm i\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}

(4.57)

the new basis elements. The charge of
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,\pm i}
under
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr},{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}})
is
(+,-)
and
(-,+)
respectively. Therefore upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}
, we find

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}=\left\{(D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}^{3}},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+i})\,,\;(D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-i})\right\}\,.

(4.58)

(4.59)

Furthermore, since in this basis
\mathcal{D}_{E}(x)=\sigma^{y}
, the 2-group action of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
:

\displaystyle D_{2}^{x}:

\displaystyle(D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}^{3}},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+i})\mapsto i(D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-i})\,,\qquad(D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-i})\mapsto-i(D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}^{3}},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+i})\,.

(4.60)

Genuine topological lines.

The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),xr^{3}}
twisted sector lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{xr},\,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{2}},\,\mathcal{E}^{xr^{3}}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
become untwisted sector lines that are charged under the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{xr}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{xr}^{3}}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}
:

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{xr},\,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{xr^{3}}
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}=\left\{\mathcal{E}_{1}^{xr}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{xr^{3}}\right\}\,,

(4.61)

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{2}}
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{2}}\,.

(4.62)

The
F
-symbols for the lines depend on the choice of discrete torsion
t\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
, whose 3 generators can be written as the
F
-symbols for each
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
subgroup of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}

[
79
]
. Writing elements in
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
as
l=(l_{\text{I}},l_{\text{II}})
, one has:

\displaystyle F_{\text{I}}(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{l},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{m},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{n})

\displaystyle=\exp\left(\frac{2\pi i}{4}\,l_{\text{I}}(m_{\text{I}}+n_{\text{I}}+[m_{\text{I}}+n_{\text{I}}])\right)\,,

(4.63)

\displaystyle F_{\text{II}}(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{l},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{m},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{n})

\displaystyle=\exp\left(\frac{2\pi i}{4}\,l_{\text{II}}(m_{\text{II}}+n_{\text{II}}+[m_{\text{II}}+n_{\text{II}}])\right)\,,

\displaystyle F_{\text{I},\text{II}}(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{l},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{m},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{n})

\displaystyle=\exp\left(\frac{2\pi i}{4}\,l_{\text{I}}(m_{\text{II}}+n_{\text{II}}+[m_{\text{II}}+n_{\text{II}}])\right)\,,

where
[m_{\text{I}}+n_{\text{I}}]\equiv(m_{\text{I}}+m_{\text{II}}\mod 2)
etc.

Surfaces that cannot end on

\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

(4.65)

D_{2}^{x}/\mathcal{A}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{xr}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{xr}^{3}}}
is in the same Schur component as the invertible surface
D_{2}^{x}
that generates the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
subsymmetry of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}

[
56
]
.

4.2.5
Neumann
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x})
and Neumann
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr})
Boundary Conditions

Since the features of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}),s}
can be deduced from those of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s}
by mapping from the first to the second presentation of
D_{8}
in equation (
4.52
), we will focus on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s}
in the following. This boundary is obtained by gauging the non-normal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
sub-symmetry of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, with possible discrete torsion
s\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
. We denote

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes{\rm SPT}_{s}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}}\,.

(4.66)

The left-cosets are:

D_{8}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}=\{(1,x),\;(r,xr^{3}),\;(r^{2},xr^{2}),\;(r^{3},xr)\}\,,

(4.67)

therefore, by picking either the first or the second representative for each coset, the symmetry after gauging can be written either as
[
56
]
:

2\mathsf{Rep}(({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),xr^{3}})\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x})\,.

(4.68)

or equivalently as

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x})\,.

(4.69)

We will use the latter presentation in the following sections.
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s}
has 1-form symmetry generated by
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
, an invertible 0-form symmetry generated by
D_{2}^{r^{2}}
and a non-invertible 0-form symmetry generated by a surface we will denote by
D_{2}^{[r]}
, which on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
was the composite object
D_{2}^{r}\oplus D_{2}^{r^{3}}
, constituting an orbit under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
. It obeys the fusion
[
56
]
:

D_{2}^{[r]}\otimes D_{2}^{[r]}=\frac{D_{2}^{\text{id}}}{D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}}\oplus\frac{D_{2}^{r^{2}}}{D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}}

(4.70)

Local operators.

Since the genuine local operator
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{x}}
at the end of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}
was untwisted and uncharged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
symmetry, it remains unaltered after gauging

(4.71)

\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{x}}
carries charge
-2
under the 0-form symmetry generated by
D_{2}^{[r]}
since on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
it had charge
-1
under both
D_{2}^{r}
and
D_{2}^{r^{3}}
.

On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, the doublet of operators
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,I}
with
I=1,2
at the end on
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
can be written in a rotated basis as

\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E\,,\pm}:=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\pm\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}\,.

(4.72)

Among these
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}
is uncharged while
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}
transforms in the non-trivial sign representation of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
. Therefore upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
, one has

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\Bigg|_{{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s}}=(\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}\,,(D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}))\,.

(4.73)

(4.74)

Both
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{+}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{-}
carry charge 0 under
D_{2}^{[r]}
and charge
-1
under
D_{2}^{r^{2}}
.

On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, the operators
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{xr}}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{xr}}
transform as
-1
under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),x}
, therefore after gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
, they become attached to the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{x}}
symmetry generator
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
.

(4.79)

the line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[r]}
is uncharged under
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
.

The SymTFT surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}
can be written as a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
orbit
D_{2}^{xr}\oplus D_{2}^{xr^{3}}
, so projects to
D_{2}^{[r]}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s}
. However, the line at its boundary is now given by
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{x[r]}
, which come from the bulk fusion
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[x]}\otimes\mathcal{E}^{[r]}
, therefore
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{x[r]}
is charged under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\widehat{x}}
.

(4.80)

The boundary
\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}),s
can be obtained from
\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s

we just described by using the
D_{8}
automorphism (
4.52
). Note that we can unitarily transform
\mathcal{D}_{E}(xr)=\sigma^{y}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\
i&0\end{pmatrix}
to
\sigma^{z}=\text{diag}(1,-1)
, denoting by

\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,\pm i}:=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\pm i\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}

(4.81)

the new basis elements. The charge of
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,\pm i}
under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}
is
\pm 1
respectively. Therefore, upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}
, we find

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\Bigg|_{{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}),s}}=\left\{\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+i}\,,\;(D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-i})\right\}\,.

(4.83)

4.2.6
Neumann
(D_{8})
Boundary Condition

We finally discuss the boundary condition obtained by gauging the full
D_{8}
0-form symmetry of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
discrete torsion
given by
\tau\in H^{3}(D_{8},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
.
The corresponding boundary condition is denoted as

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(D_{8}),\tau}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes{\rm SPT}_{\tau}}{D_{8}}\,.

(4.84)

The symmetry on this boundary is
\mathcal{S}=2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
, generated by topological lines
D_{1}^{R}
, for
R\in\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
. All surfaces are condensation defects of condensable algebras in
\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
.

Non-genuine local operators.

When gauging the full
D_{8}
symmetry, since all
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
SymTFT lines transform non-trivially, they give rise to twisted sector local operators and there are no genuine local operators on this boundary.

(4.86)

whose
F
-symbols follow from
\tau\in H^{3}(D_{8},U(1))
. The charge of these lines under the
\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
1-form symmetry generators is:

\text{Link}(D_{1}^{R},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[g]})=\chi_{R}([g])\,,

(4.87)

where
\chi_{R}
is the character of the irrep
R
.
There are no twisted sector lines since all SymTFT surfaces can end on this boundary.

4.3
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
Gapped Phases

The minimal gapped phases for
D_{8}
0-form symmetry in 2+1d follow of course the standard Landau paradigm, plus SPTs. Nevertheless we will start with this well-known class of gapped phases, as we will use it to then gauge on the symmetry boundary in order to get the remaining phases for the less well-studied, categorical symmetries.
A summary can be seen in table
7
.

\begin{array}[]{|c|l|}\hline\cr\text{Physical BC $\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}$}&{\bm{Q}}_{p}\text{ with Dirichlet BCs}\cr\hline\cr\hline\cr{\rm Dir}&\text{$D_{8}$ SSB: 8 vacua}\cr\hline\cr\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}),s&{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\ \text{SSB, 4 vacua}\cr\hline\cr\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p&{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\ \text{SSB, 2 vacua}\cr\hline\cr\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t&{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\ \text{SSB, 2 vacua}\cr\hline\cr\ \text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{2}}),t&{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\ \text{SSB, 2 vacua}\cr\hline\cr\ \text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s&{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\ \text{SSB, 4 vacua}\cr\hline\cr\ \text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}),s&{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\ \text{SSB, 4 vacua}\cr\hline\cr\ \text{Neu}(D_{8}),\tau&\text{SPTs}\cr\hline\cr\end{array}

Table 7:
Summary of minimal gapped phases for
2\mathsf{Vec}(D_{8})
.

4.3.1
D_{8}
SSB Phase

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\,.

(4.88)

In this case all local operators
\mathcal{O}^{R}
can end with multiplicity
\text{dim}R
, yielding
\sum_{R}(\text{dim}R)^{2}=|G|
many vacua, in this case 8. Setting
H=1
in equation (
2.48
), they are:

\displaystyle v_{1}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{8}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

(4.89)

\displaystyle v_{xr}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{8}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{xr^{3}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{8}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{r^{2}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{8}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{x}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{8}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{r}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{8}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{r^{3}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{8}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{xr^{2}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{8}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}\right)\,.

The action of
g\in D_{8}
on each vacuum is

g\cdot v_{\bar{g}}=v_{g\bar{g}}\,,

(4.90)

from which we see that no vacuum is invariant an that the full
D_{8}
0-form symmetry is spontaneously broken so this is a
D_{8}
SSB phase. We can summarize this as:

2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
:
D_{8}
SSB Phase

\bigoplus_{g\in D_{8}}{\rm Triv}_{g}\,,\qquad D_{2}^{g}:{\text{Triv}_{g^{\prime}}\mapsto{\text{Triv}_{gg^{\prime}}}}

(4.91)

4.3.2
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB Phase

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}),s}\,.

(4.92)

The vacua are:

\displaystyle v_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}=v_{1}+v_{r^{2}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}\right)\,,

(4.93)

\displaystyle v_{xr{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}=v_{xr}+v_{xr^{3}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{x{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}=v_{x}+v_{xr^{2}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{r{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}=v_{r}+v_{r^{3}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}\right)\,.

This is
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB phase, in which the action of the generators is as follows:

\displaystyle x:

\displaystyle v_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}

\displaystyle\longleftrightarrow v_{x{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}\,,

\displaystyle v_{r{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}

\displaystyle\longleftrightarrow v_{xr{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}\,,

(4.94)

\displaystyle r:

\displaystyle v_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}

\displaystyle\longleftrightarrow v_{r{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}\,,

\displaystyle v_{x{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}

\displaystyle\longleftrightarrow v_{xr{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}\,.

In summary we obtain the following TQFT:

2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB phase

\text{Triv}_{1}\oplus\text{Triv}_{2}\oplus\text{Triv}_{3}\oplus\text{Triv}_{4}:\qquad r=1_{13}\oplus 1_{31}\oplus 1_{24}\oplus 1_{42}\,,\ x=1_{12}\oplus 1_{21}\oplus 1_{34}\oplus 1_{43}\,.

(4.95)

4.3.3
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB Phase I

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p}\,.

(4.96)

The vacua are:

\displaystyle v_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}}=v_{1}+v_{r}+v_{r^{2}}+v_{r^{3}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}\right)\,,

(4.97)

\displaystyle v_{x{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}}=v_{x}+v_{xr}+v_{xr^{2}}+v_{xr^{3}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{r}}\right)\,.

This is
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB phase, in which
x
exchanges the two vacua:

2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB Phase
I

\text{Triv}_{1}\oplus\text{Triv}_{2}:\qquad x=1_{12}\oplus 1_{21}\,.

(4.98)

4.3.4
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB Phase II

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}),t}\,.

(4.99)

The vacua are:

\displaystyle v_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}}=v_{1}+v_{xr}+v_{r^{2}}+v_{xr^{3}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}\right)\,,

(4.100)

\displaystyle v_{x{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{3}}}=v_{x}+v_{r}+v_{xr^{2}}+v_{r^{3}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}\right)\,.

This is
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB phase, in which
x
exchanges the two vacua.

4.3.5
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}
SSB Phase

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{2}}),t}\,.

(4.101)

The vacua are:

\displaystyle v_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{2}}}=v_{1}+v_{x}+v_{r^{2}}+v_{xr^{2}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}\right)\,,

(4.102)

\displaystyle v_{xr{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{2}}}=v_{xr}+v_{r^{3}}+v_{xr^{3}}+v_{r}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}\right)\,.

This is
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}
SSB phase, in which
xr
exchanges the two vacua.

4.3.6
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
SSB Phase I

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s}\,.

(4.103)

The vacua are:

\displaystyle v_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}}=v_{1}+v_{x}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

(4.104)

\displaystyle v_{r{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}}=v_{r}+v_{xr^{3}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{r^{2}{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}}=v_{r^{2}}+v_{xr^{2}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{r^{3}{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}}=v_{r^{3}}+v_{xr}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

In this phase
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}
cyclically permutes the vacua:

r=1_{12}\oplus 1_{23}\oplus 1_{34}\oplus 1_{41}

(4.105)

2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
SSB Phase I

\text{Triv}_{1}\oplus\text{Triv}_{2}\oplus\text{Triv}_{3}\oplus\text{Triv}_{4}:\qquad r=1_{12}\oplus 1_{23}\oplus 1_{34}\oplus 1_{41}\,.

(4.106)

4.3.7
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
SSB Phase II

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}),s}\,.

(4.107)

The vacua are:

\displaystyle v_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}}=v_{1}+v_{xr}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

(4.108)

\displaystyle v_{r{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}}=v_{r}+v_{x}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{r^{2}{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}}=v_{r^{2}}+v_{xr^{3}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{r^{3}{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}}=v_{r^{3}}+v_{xr^{2}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,1}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,1,2}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,2,1}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2,2}\right)\,.

In this phase
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}
cyclically permutes the vacua in the same way as (
4.106
)

4.3.8
D_{8}
SPT Phase

Choosing

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(D_{8}),\tau}\,,

(4.109)

there is a single vacuum:

v_{D_{8}}=\sum_{\bar{g}\in D_{8}}v_{\bar{g}}v_{\bar{g}}=1

(4.110)

in which the full
D_{8}
symmetry is preserved. The SPT phase is labeled by

\tau\in H^{3}(D_{8},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,.

(4.111)

4.4
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
Gapped Phases

Let us now fix the symmetry boundary of the SymTFT to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s}\,,

(4.112)

which carries the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
symmetry on it. As discussed in section
4.2.5
, this boundary condition is obtained by gauging the non-normal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
subgroup of
D_{8}={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
The symmetry structure of
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
comprises of a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
invertible subsymmetry generated by
(D_{1}^{\widehat{x}},D_{2}^{r^{2}})
along with a non-invertible 0-form symmetry generated by
D_{2}^{[r]}
with fusion rule

D_{2}^{[r]}\otimes D_{2}^{[r]}=D_{2}^{C}\otimes(D_{2}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{2}^{r^{2}})\,,

(4.113)

where
D_{2}^{C}:=D_{2}^{\text{id}}/(D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{x}})
is the condensation defect for
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
.

4.4.1
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB Phase

Taking the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\,,

(4.114)

the SymTFT lines that have untwisted ends on both
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
are:

\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\}\,,

(4.115)

On
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
has one untwisted end

{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}={\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,1}+{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,2}
and one
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
twisted end
{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,-}={\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,1}-{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,2}
.
Compactifying the SymTFT, one thus obtains a four dimensional space of untwisted local operators spanned by

\left\{1\,,\;\mathcal{O}^{E,1}\,,\;\mathcal{O}^{E,2}\,,\;\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}\right\}\,,

(4.116)

where
\mathcal{O}^{E,j}
for
j=1,2
denotes the local operator obtained by compactifying
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
with the ends
{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,j}
on the symmetry and physical boundary respectively

(4.118)

The idempotents can be computed by starting with the
D_{8}
SSB phase for
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
of section
4.3.1
(which has the same
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
as our current sandwich) and gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
symmetry on the symmetry boundary for
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
to obtain the symmetry
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
we are interested in. They are:

\displaystyle v_{0}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,1}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,2}\right)\,,

(4.119)

\displaystyle v_{1}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1,}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{2}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,1}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,2}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{3}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+2i\mathcal{O}^{E,1}-2i\mathcal{O}^{E,2}\right)\,,

We obtain a
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
phase with four vacua.

D_{2}^{r^{2}}
acts by
-1
on both
\mathcal{O}^{E,1}
and
\mathcal{O}^{E,2}
so it permutes the vacua in pairs:

D_{2}^{r^{2}}=1_{02}\oplus 1_{20}\oplus 1_{13}\oplus 1_{31}\,.

(4.120)

To compute the action of the non-invertible symmetry
D_{2}^{[r]}
, we recall that
D_{2}^{[r]}
descends from
D_{2}^{r}\oplus D_{2}^{r^{3}}
upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
. The sphere linking action of
D_{2}^{r}\oplus D_{2}^{r^{3}}
on
\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}
is
-1-1=-2
while on
\mathcal{O}^{E,1}
and
\mathcal{O}^{E,2}
it is given by
i-i=0
. Therefore, the non-invertible
D_{2}^{[r]}
sends each vacuum into the sum of two others:

D_{2}^{[r]}=1_{01}\oplus 1_{03}\oplus 1_{12}\oplus 1_{10}\oplus 1_{23}\oplus 1_{21}\oplus 1_{30}\oplus 1_{32}\,.

(4.121)

Since
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
has no (non-identity) genuine lines,
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
is realized trivially in each vacuum.
It can be easily verified that the fusion rule (
4.113
) holds, by using the fact that

D_{2}^{C}=2\times(1_{00}\oplus 1_{11}\oplus 1_{22}\oplus 1_{33})

(4.122)

since the 1-form symmetry is generated by the identity line
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}\simeq D_{1}^{1}
in each vacuum.
In summary, this is a
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB with 4 vacua:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
is preserved in each so this is a confining phase,
D_{2}^{r^{2}}
is spontaneously broken and swaps pairs of vacua, while
D_{2}^{[r]}
sends each vacuum to the sum of two others, eq. (
4.121
).

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB with Trivial
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
(Confining Phase)

\text{Triv}_{0}\oplus\text{Triv}_{1}\oplus\text{Triv}_{2}\oplus\text{Triv}_{3}:\qquad\left\{\begin{aligned} {\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}:&\quad 1_{02}\oplus 1_{20}\oplus 1_{13}\oplus 1_{31}\cr D_{2}^{[r]}:&\quad 1_{01}\oplus 1_{03}\oplus 1_{12}\oplus 1_{10}\oplus 1_{23}\oplus 1_{21}\oplus 1_{30}\oplus 1_{32}\cr D_{2}^{C}:&\quad 2\times(1_{00}\oplus 1_{11}\oplus 1_{22}\oplus 1_{33})\cr{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}:&\quad\text{trivial}\,.\end{aligned}\right.

(4.123)

4.4.2
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB Phase

Let us take the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}),s^{\prime}}\,.

(4.124)

The SymTFT lines that have untwisted ends on both
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
are:

\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}\}\,,

(4.125)

which, after compactifying the SymTFT, give rise to a two dimensional space of untwisted local operators spanned by

\left\{1\,,\;\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}\right\}\,,

(4.126)

where
\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}
comes from
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}
ending on both boundaries

(4.127)

The idempotents can be computed by starting with the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB phase for
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
of section
4.3.2
(which has the same
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
as our current sandwich) and gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
on the symmetry boundary. They are:

\displaystyle v_{0}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}})\,,

(4.128)

\displaystyle v_{1}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}})\,.

This is a
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
phase with two vacua.

The only non-trivial line on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
is
\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{r^{2}}
(coming from the SymTFT surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
), which gives rise to a
D_{2}^{r^{2}}
twisted sector line after compactification:

(D_{2}^{r^{2}}\,,\mathcal{L}^{r^{2}})=\left((D_{2}^{r^{2}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{2}})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{r^{2}}\right)\,.

(4.130)

\mathcal{L}^{r^{2}}
is uncharged under
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
: the 1-form symmetry is therefore realized trivially in each vacuum.

Let us turn to the 0-form symmetry:

D_{2}^{r^{2}}
is the identity

D_{2}^{r^{2}}=1_{00}\oplus 1_{11}\,,

(4.131)

whereas the non-invertible
D_{2}^{[r]}
is non-trivial, since
\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}
carries charge
-1-1=-2
under
D_{2}^{r}\oplus D_{2}^{r^{3}}
. Under this symmetry action, the two vacua are thus exchanged and multiplied by a factor of 2:

D_{2}^{[r]}=2\times(1_{01}\oplus 1_{10})

(4.132)

One can verify the fusion rule (
4.113
) using the fact that

D_{2}^{C}=2\times(1_{00}\oplus 1_{11})

(4.133)

This is therefore a
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB Phase since the invertible
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
is preserved and only the
D_{2}^{[r]}
non-invertible symmetry of
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
is spontaneously broken.

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB (Confining Phase)

\text{Triv}_{0}\oplus\text{Triv}_{1}:\qquad\left\{\begin{aligned} {\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}:&\quad\text{trivial}\cr D_{2}^{[r]}:&\quad 2\times(1_{01}\oplus 1_{10})\cr D_{2}^{C}:&\quad 2\times(1_{00}\oplus 1_{11})\cr{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}:&\quad\text{trivial}\,.\end{aligned}\right.

(4.134)

4.4.3
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SPT Phase with trivial
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}

Let us take the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}),p}\,.

(4.135)

The SymTFT line that has untwisted ends on both
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
is only the identity
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}
,
which, after compactifying the SymTFT gives rise to a single local operator and thus one vacuum. The lines on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
are
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{r^{2}}
, eq. (
4.129
), and
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[r]}
, which gives rise to a
D_{2}^{[r]}
twisted sector line after compactification:

(D_{2}^{[r]}\,,\mathcal{L}^{[r]})=\left((D_{2}^{[r]}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[r]})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[r]}\right)\,,

(4.136)

(4.137)

Both
\mathcal{E}^{r^{2}}
and
\mathcal{E}^{[r]}
are uncharged under
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
: the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry is therefore realized trivially.

The idempotents can be computed by starting with the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB phase I for
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
of section
4.3.3
(which has the same
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
as our current sandwich) and gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
on the symmetry boundary, confirming that in the thus obtained
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
symmetric phase there is a single one vacuum
v_{0}
with
D_{2}^{r^{2}}
realized trivially and

D_{2}^{[r]}\cong 2\times 1_{00}

(4.138)

such that a line living at the end of
D_{2}^{[r]}
is not charged under
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
.

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:

SPT Phase and Trivial

(Confining Phase)

(4.139)

4.4.4
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
Mixed SPT Phase

Taking the physical boundary to be

the SymTFT line that has untwisted ends on both

(4.145)

Unlike the previous phase,
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{x[r]}
is charged under
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
, therefore the 1-form symmetry is realized non-trivially this is a mixed ‘non-trivial SPT’ phase between the 1-form symmetry and
D_{2}^{[r]}
since there is a non-genuine line (in the twisted sector for the non-invertible
D_{2}^{[r]}
0-form symm) which is charged under the 1-form symm generated by
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
: it is the higher-dimensional analogue of the string order-parameters for 1+1d SPTs. No SymTFT surfaces end on both boundaries, so there are no genuine line operators in this phase.

The idempotents can be computed by starting with the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
SSB phase II for
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
of section
4.3.4
(which has the same
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
as our current sandwich) and gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
on the symmetry boundary, confirming that in the thus obtained
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
symmetric phase there is a single one vacuum
v_{0}
with
D_{2}^{r^{2}}
realized trivially and

D_{2}^{[r]}\cong 2\times 1_{00}

(4.146)

such that a line living at the end of
D_{2}^{[r]}
is charged under
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
.

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
Mixed SPT Phase with non-trivial
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}

(4.147)

4.4.5
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
SSB Phase

Let us take the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr^{2}}),t}\,.

(4.148)

The SymTFT lines that have untwisted ends on both
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
are:

\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}\}\,,

(4.149)

which, after compactifying the SymTFT, give rise to a two dimensional space of untwisted local operators spanned by

\left\{1\,,\;\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}\right\}\,,

(4.150)

where
\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}
comes from
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}
ending on both boundaries

(4.153)

\mathcal{L}^{x}
is charged under
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
, obeys
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
fusion rules and has F-symbols given by
s-s^{\prime}\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,U(1))
.

The idempotents are the same as those of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}
SSB phase for
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
of section
4.3.5
(which has the same
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
as our current sandwich) since both vacua are already invariant under
x
:

\displaystyle v_{0}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}\right)\,,

(4.154)

\displaystyle v_{1}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}\right)\,.

However, the effect of gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
is visible at the level of lines: after gauging each of the two invariant vacua
v_{0}
,
v_{1}
carry
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with a 3-cocycle twist
s-s^{\prime}\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
, i.e. toric code or double semion, so the underlying 3d TFT is

\mathfrak{T}=\left(\text{DW}_{s-s^{\prime}}\right)_{0}\oplus\left(\text{DW}_{s-s^{\prime}}\right)_{1}

(4.155)

with line operators given by
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
, which is bosonic, and
\mathcal{L}^{x}
which is a boson if
s-s^{\prime}
is trivial or a semion otherwise.
The invertible 0-form symmetry generator
D_{2}^{r^{2}}
is the identity for
\mathfrak{T}
, while
non-invertible
D_{2}^{[r]}
is realized as

D_{2}^{[r]}=(D_{2}^{C})_{01}\oplus(D_{2}^{C})_{10}

(4.156)

which obeys the fusion (
4.113
).

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
SSB Phase

4.4.6
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB Phase

Let us now take the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),s^{\prime}}\,.

(4.159)

which is the same as
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
(upto discrete torsion). The SymTFT lines that end are:

\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\}\,,

(4.160)

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
has one untwisted end

{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}={\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,1}+{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,2}
and one
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
twisted end
{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,-}={\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,1}-{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,2}
.
Compactifying the SymTFT, one thus obtains a three dimensional space of untwisted local operators spanned by

\left\{1\,,\;\mathcal{O}^{E,+}\,,\;\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}\right\}\,,

(4.161)

where
\mathcal{O}^{E,+}
denotes the local operator obtained by compactifying
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
with end
{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}
on both SymTFT boundaries

(4.165)

\mathcal{L}^{x}
is charged under
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
, obeys
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
fusion rules and has F-symbols given by
s-s^{\prime}\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,U(1))
.
The idempotents can be computed by starting with the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}
SSB phase I for
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
of section
4.3.6
(which has the same
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
as our current sandwich) and gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
on the symmetry boundary. They are:

\displaystyle v_{0}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}+2\mathcal{O}^{E,+}\right)\,,

(4.166)

\displaystyle v_{1}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}-2\mathcal{O}^{E,+}\right)\,,

\displaystyle v_{2}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{1_{x}}\right)\,.

v_{0}
and
v_{1}
were already
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
symmetric so, after gauging it, they carry a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with a 3-cocycle twist
s-s^{\prime}\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
, i.e. toric code or double semion, whereas
v_{2}
comes from the orbit of two vacua which were not
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
invariant so after gauging its underline TFT is therefore trivial. In total, the underlying 3d TFT for this
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
symmetric phase is

\mathfrak{T}=\left(\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{s-s^{\prime}}\right)_{0}\oplus\left(\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{s-s^{\prime}}\right)_{1}\oplus{\rm Triv}_{2}

(4.167)

with line operators in the DW theories given by
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
, which is bosonic, and
\mathcal{L}^{x}
which is a boson if
s-s^{\prime}
is trivial or a semion otherwise.
Since
\mathcal{O}^{E,+}
carries charge
-1
under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),r^{2}}
, the invertible 0-form symmetry generator
D_{2}^{r^{2}}
is realized as

D_{2}^{r^{2}}=1_{01}\oplus 1_{10}\oplus 1_{22}\,.

(4.168)

\mathcal{O}^{E,+}
carries charge 0 under the non-invertible
D_{2}^{[r]}
therefore its action on the vacua is

D_{2}^{[r]}:(v_{0}\,,\;v_{1}\,,\;v_{2})\longmapsto(v_{2}\,,\;v_{2}\,,\;2v_{0}+2v_{1})\,.

(4.169)

and this surface operator is realized concretely as

D_{2}^{[r]}=B_{02}\oplus B_{12}\oplus\overline{B}_{20}\oplus\overline{B}_{21}\,,

(4.170)

where
B_{i2}
for
i=0,1
is the interface between
\left({\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})}_{s-s^{\prime}}\right)_{i}
and
{\rm Triv}_{2}
while
\overline{B}_{2i}
is the converse interface.
One can verify (
4.113
) by using the fact that the product of two
B
interfaces is a condensation.

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB Phase (“Superstar”)

4.4.7
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
SSB Phase with mixed SPT

Taking the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}),s^{\prime}}\,,

(4.173)

the SymTFT lines that end are:

\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\}\,,

(4.174)

Compactifying the SymTFT, one thus obtains a two dimensional space of untwisted local operators spanned by

\left\{1\,,\;\mathcal{O}^{E,+}\right\}\,,

(4.175)

where
\mathcal{O}^{E,+}
denotes the local operator obtained by compactifying
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
with end
{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{E,+}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and
\mathcal{E}^{+i}
(where
i
is the 4
th
root of unity) on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
, recall eq. (
4.82
).

There are non-trivial twisted sector local operators: for example, the compactification of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}}
produces a local operator attached to the
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
line.

(D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}\,,\mathcal{O}^{1_{xr}})=\left((D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}\,,{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{1_{xr}})\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{0}^{1_{xr}}\right)\,.

(4.179)

\mathcal{E}_{1}^{x[r]}
is charged under
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
, therefore the 1-form symmetry is realized non-trivially, like for the phase in sec.
4.4.4
. No SymTFT surfaces end on both boundaries, so there are no genuine line operators.

The idempotents can be computed by starting with the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}
SSB phase II for
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
of section
4.3.7
(which has the same
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
as our current sandwich) and gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
on the symmetry boundary. They are:

\displaystyle v_{0}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1+\mathcal{O}^{E,+}\right)\,,

(4.180)

\displaystyle v_{1}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\mathcal{O}^{E,+}\right)\,.

Both vacua come from the orbit of two vacua which were not
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
invariant so the underlying 3d TFT in each vacuum is trivial

\mathfrak{T}=\text{Triv}_{0}\oplus\text{Triv}_{1}\,.

(4.181)

D_{2}^{r^{2}}
exchanges the two vacua, since
\mathcal{O}^{E,+}
carries charge
-1
under it:

D_{2}^{r^{2}}=1_{01}\oplus 1_{10}\,.

(4.182)

This is therefore a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
SSB phase in which the non-invertible 0-form symmetry sends ecah vacua to the sum of both:

D_{2}^{[r]}=1_{00}\oplus 1_{01}\oplus 1_{10}\oplus 1_{11}\,.

(4.183)

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
:
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
SSB with non-trivial
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}

\text{Triv}_{0}\oplus\text{Triv}_{1}:\qquad\left\{\begin{aligned} {\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}:&\quad D_{2}^{r^{2}}=1_{01}\oplus 1_{10}\cr D_{2}^{[r]}:&\quad 1_{00}\oplus 1_{01}\oplus 1_{10}\oplus 1_{11}\cr D_{2}^{C}:&\quad 2\times(1_{00}\oplus 1_{11})\cr{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}:&\quad\text{non-trivial}\,.\end{aligned}\right.

(4.184)

4.4.8
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB Phase

Let us finally take the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(D_{8}),\tau}\,.

(4.185)

Since no SymTFT lines end on both boundaries, there is only the single identity local operator in the IR TQFT describing this gapped phase.

The SymTFT surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
ending on both boundaries produces a genuine line operator

\mathcal{L}^{x}=\left(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{x}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}\,,\widetilde{\mathcal{E}}_{1}^{[x]}\right)\,,

(4.186)

depicted as

({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

(4.188)

4.5
2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
Gapped Phases

We now describe the minimal gapped phases obtained by choosing the symmetry boundary

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(D_{8})}\,,

(4.191)

described in section
4.2.6
, with trivial discrete torsion
\tau\in H^{3}(D_{8},U(1))
. The symmetry is
\mathcal{S}=2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
, i.e.
\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
1-form symmetry generated by lines
D_{1}^{R}
, for
R\in\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
:

D_{1}^{1}\,,\quad D_{1}^{1_{x}}\,,\quad D_{1}^{1_{r}}\,,\quad D_{1}^{1_{xr}}\,,\quad D_{1}^{E}\,.

(4.192)

Their fusions follow from the tensor products of irreps, consistently with the
D_{8}
character table
5
and are (for
1_{k}=1_{x}\,,\;1_{r}\,,\;1_{xr}
):

\displaystyle D_{1}^{1_{x}}\otimes D_{1}^{1_{r}}

\displaystyle=D_{1}^{1_{xr}}\,,\quad D_{1}^{1_{k}}\otimes D_{1}^{1_{k}}=D_{1}^{1}\,,

(4.193)

\displaystyle D_{1}^{E}\otimes D_{1}^{E}

\displaystyle=D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{1_{x}}\oplus D_{1}^{1_{r}}\oplus D_{1}^{1_{xr}}\,,

from which we see that the 1-dimensional irreps comprise of an invertible
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry, whereas
D_{1}^{E}
is non-invertible. (1+1)d gapped and gapless phases with
\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
categorical symmetry were studied from the SymTFT in
[
40
]
and from the lattice in
[
80
]
.

We recall that on the
2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
symmetry boundary in (2+1)d all local operators are non-genuine: this implies that all
2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
-symmetric gapped phases will have a unique vacuum.

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
carries genuine lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[g]}
coming from the end of the bulk SymTFT surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}
, with charge

\text{Link}(D_{1}^{R},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[g]})=\chi_{R}([g])\,,

(4.194)

under
D_{1}^{R}
for
R\in\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
. The non-identity SymTFT surfaces that also end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
will in general give rise to line order parameters charged under certain sub-symmetries of
\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
, revealing 1-form symmetry spontaneous symmetry breaking, as will see below.

4.5.1
2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
Trivial Phase

Consider the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\,.

(4.195)

The idempotents can be computed by starting with the
D_{8}
SSB phase for
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
of section
4.3.1
(which has the same
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
as our current sandwich) and gauging
D_{8}
0-form symmetry on the symmetry boundary. Since the
D_{8}
symmetry is completely broken, after gauging we obtain a single vacuum whose underlying TFT is trivial.

The only genuine line in this phase is the identity, so any representation
R
just acts as
{\text{dim}}(R)
copies of the identity line.
This phase has a non-invertible 1-form symmetry
\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
which is preserved. The associated line operators (charges) are confined.

2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
: Trivial Phase with trivial
\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
1-form symmetry (Confining Phase)

4.5.2
2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})/2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

Let us take the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}),s}\,.

(4.198)

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}

D_{8}

D_{8}

{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}

, denoted as DW
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{s}
, i.e. toric code or double semion.

The SymTFT bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
ending on both boundaries produces, after compactification, a genuine line
\mathcal{L}^{r^{2}}
charged under
D_{1}^{E}
which is realized in this phase as:

D_{1}^{E}\simeq 2D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}\,,

(4.199)

where
D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
is the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
electric line in DW
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{s}
linking non-trivially with
\mathcal{L}^{x}
. The remaining
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
sub-symmetry of
\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
, generated by
D_{1}^{1_{x}},\;D_{1}^{1_{r}}
is preserved in this phase.

2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
:

4.5.3
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
SSB Phase I

Let us take the physical boundary to be

(4.202)

The idempotents can be computed by starting with the

of section
4.3.3

{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}

({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})_{p}

{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}

D_{1}^{\widehat{r}}

The SymTFT bulk surfaces
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}

\mathcal{L}^{r^{2}}\,,\;\mathcal{L}^{r}\,,\;\mathcal{L}^{r^{3}}

\mathcal{L}^{r}

\mathcal{L}^{r^{3}}

-1
under
D_{1}^{1_{x}}
and
D_{1}^{1_{xr}}

+1

D_{1}^{1_{r}}
. The charge of
\mathcal{L}^{r}
and
\mathcal{L}^{r^{3}}
under
D_{1}^{E}
is
0
while that of
\mathcal{L}^{r^{2}}
is
-2
. The
2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
symmetry generators are therefore realized in this phase as follows:

\displaystyle D_{1}^{1_{r}}

\displaystyle\simeq D_{1}^{1}\,,\quad

(4.203)

\displaystyle D_{1}^{1_{x}}

\displaystyle\simeq D_{1}^{1_{xr}}\simeq D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}\,,

\displaystyle D_{1}^{E}

\displaystyle\simeq D_{1}^{\widehat{r}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{3}}\,,

so it is a
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
SSB phase for the 1-form symmetry generated by
D_{1}^{1_{x}}
and
D_{1}^{1_{xr}}
.

and the lines generating its electric
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry as
D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}
and
D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}
.

The SymTFT bulk surfaces
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
ending on both boundaries produce, after compactification, genuine lines
\mathcal{L}^{r^{2}}\,,\;\mathcal{L}^{x}\,,\;\mathcal{L}^{xr^{2}}
. From the SymTFT bulk linking, we know that
\mathcal{L}^{x}
and
\mathcal{L}^{xr^{2}}
carry charge
-1
under
D_{1}^{1_{r}}
and
D_{1}^{1_{xr}}
, charge
+1
under
D_{1}^{1_{x}}
and
0
under
D_{1}^{E}
.
\mathcal{L}^{r^{2}}
is charged only under
D_{1}^{E}
, with linking equal to
-2
.
The
2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
symmetry generators are therefore realized in this phase as follows:

\displaystyle D_{1}^{1_{x}}

\displaystyle\simeq D_{1}^{1}\,,\quad

(4.211)

\displaystyle D_{1}^{1_{r}}

\displaystyle\simeq D_{1}^{1_{xr}}\simeq D_{1}^{\widehat{x}}\,,

\displaystyle D_{1}^{E}

\displaystyle\simeq D_{1}^{\widehat{r}^{2}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{xr}^{2}}\,,

so it is a
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
SSB phase for the 1-form symmetry generated by
D_{1}^{1_{r}}
and
D_{1}^{1_{xr}}
.

2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

4.5.8
2\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
SSB Phase

Let us finally take the physical boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(D_{8}),\tau}\,.

(4.222)

Finally the F-symbols of the charged lines
\mathcal{L}^{[g]}
are controlled by the 3-cocycle
\tau\in H^{3}(D_{8},U(1))
.
This gapped phase is the
D_{8}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with a
\tau
3-cocycle twist.
