5
Minimal and Non-Minimal SSB Phases for
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})

In the past sections, we encountered one particularly interesting gapped phase, which is the SSB Phase for
\mathcal{S}=2\mathsf{Rep}(\mathbb{G}^{(2)})
, where the 2-group symmetry is

\mathbb{G}^{(2)}={\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}\,,

(5.1)

for
n=3\,,4
, which we discussed in sections
3.5.3
and
4.4.6
, and dubbed “superstar phases”.
We will generalize this now to higher
n
.
In this section, we provide an alternate route to this gapped phase via a direct gauging of a certain SSB phase with
2\mathsf{Vec}(S_{3})
and
2\mathsf{Vec}(D_{8})
respectively.
This allows for an immediate generalization to the case where
n>4
as well as to non-minimal generalizations of this phase.

5.1
Minimal SSB Phases

In general, the symmetry category
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
can be obtained from
2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(0)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
by gauging the non-normal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
sub-symmetry.
Specifically, the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB phase corresponds to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(0)}
SSB phase with
2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(0)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
.
We now describe this
{\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(0)}
SSB in
2\mathsf{Vec}(D_{2n}^{(0)})
symmetric systems for different
n
and directly perform its gauging.

•

\bm{n=3}
: Let us begin with the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
SSB phase realized in
S_{3}=D_{6}={\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\rtimes Z_{2}
symmetric systems.
This gapped phase has 3 indistinguishable vacua.
These vacua are permuted by the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetry generated by
D_{2}^{a}
and each vacuum preserves one
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry (generated by
D_{2}^{b}
,
D_{2}^{ab}
or
D_{2}^{a^{2}b}
).
There are in fact two distinct
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
SSB phases labeled by
t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,U(1))
corresponding to the SPT nature of the preserved
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
in each vacuum.
Now lets consider gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
symmetry.
Once we single out
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, the vacua are in fact distinguishable.
We depict the vacua as the vertices of a triangle:

(5.2)

The vacuum
v_{0}
is invariant under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
while
v_{1}
and
v_{-1}
are exchanged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
action.
Therefore the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
SSB phase realizes the phase

{\rm Triv}_{0}\oplus{\rm SSB}_{\pm 1}\,.

(5.3)

Once we gauge
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, the trivial vacuum
v_{0}
maps to the vacuum where the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry is spontaneously broken or equivalently this vacuum realizes a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
topological order.
For
t=+1
, this is the toric code topological order while for
t=-1
, it is the double semion topological order.
Specifically the end of the
D_{2}^{b}
surface (whose associator is determined by
t
) in the
v_{0}
vacuum becomes a topological line that is charged under the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry.
Conversely, the vacua
v_{\pm 1}
become a single vacuum
v_{[1]}
in the gauged theory that realizes the trivial phase for the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry.
Finally the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
generators
D_{2}^{a}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{2}}
combine into a non-invertible symmetry operator
D_{2}^{A}
whose action can be inferred from its action on
v_{j}
.

D_{2}^{A}:(v_{0}\,,v_{[1]})\longmapsto(v_{[1]}\,,2v_{0}+v_{[1]})\,.

(5.4)

This is precisely the symmetry action that was previously obtained from the SymTFT construction of gapped phases in section
3.5.3
.

{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
SSB phase.
We present
D_{8}

D_{8}=\langle a\,,b\ |a^{4}=b^{2}=1\,,bab=a^{3}\rangle\,.

(5.8)

The vacua
v_{0}
and
v_{2}
are dual to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
symmetric vacua and therefore spontaneously break the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry, realizing the
t
-
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
topological gauge theory, i.e., Toric Code or Double Semion for
t=+1
or
-1
respectively.
While
v_{[1]}
is dual the the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
SSB vacua
v_{\pm 1}
, therefore realizes a trivial phase for the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry.

The full symmetry category after gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
is
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
.
In addition to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry, this category contains invertible and a non-invertible 0-form generators (upto condensations), which descend from
D_{2}^{a^{2}}
and
D_{2}^{a}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{3}}
respectively.
We will denote these as
D_{2}^{a^{2}}
and
D_{2}^{A}
respectively.
Their fusion rules are
[
56
]

\begin{split}D_{2}^{a^{2}}\otimes D_{2}^{a^{2}}&=D_{2}^{\text{id}}\,,\\
D_{2}^{a^{2}}\otimes D_{2}^{A}&=D_{2}^{A}\,,\\
D_{2}^{A}\otimes D_{2}^{A}&=\frac{D_{2}^{\text{id}}}{D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}}\oplus\frac{D_{2}^{a^{2}}}{D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}}\,,\end{split}

(5.9)

where
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
is the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry generator.
The action of the 0-form symmetries in
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
can be obtained from the action of the lifted symmetries in
2\mathsf{Vec}(D_{8})
.

\begin{split}D_{2}^{a^{2}}:(v_{0}\,,v_{[1]}\,,v_{2})&\longmapsto(v_{2}\,,v_{[1]}\,,v_{0})\,,\\
D_{2}^{A}:(v_{0}\,,v_{[1]}\,,v_{2})&\longmapsto(v_{[1]}\,,2v_{0}+2v_{2}\,,v_{[1]})\,,\\
\end{split}

(5.10)

In summary, we obtain a phase with 3 vacua, 2 of which are topologically ordered while the third is topologically trivial and there is an action of a non-invertible 2-categorical symmetry that stabilizes this phase structure.

•

\bm{n=2\ell+1}:
To obtain the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell+1}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB phase, our starting point will be a
D_{4\ell+2}={\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell+1}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form symmetric theory that realizes the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell+1}
SSB phase.
We present
D_{4\ell+2}
as

D_{4\ell+2}=\langle a\,,b\ |a^{2\ell+1}=b^{2}=1\,,bab=a^{2\ell}\rangle\,.

(5.11)

This phase has
2\ell+1
vacua labeled as
v_{j}
with

(5.12)

In terms of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
symmetry, the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell+1}
SSB phase splits as

{\rm Triv}_{0}\bigoplus_{j=1}^{\ell}{\rm SSB}_{\pm j}\,.

(5.13)

{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
we obtain the phase with
\ell+1
vacua summarized as

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell+1}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell+1}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
SSB Phase

\left[{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{t}\right]_{0}\ \bigoplus_{j=1}^{\ell}\ {\rm Triv}_{[j]}\,.

(5.14)

(5.15)

The symmetry category
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell+1}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
contains
\ell
non-invertible symmetry defects that descend from
D_{2}^{a^{p}}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{-p}}
upong gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
.
We denote the symmetry operator thus obtained as
D_{2}^{A,p}
.
The fusion rules of these is

D_{2}^{A,p}\oplus D_{2}^{A,p^{\prime}}=D_{2}^{A,p+p^{\prime}}\oplus D_{2}^{A,p-p^{\prime}}\,,

(5.16)

where we use the identification

\begin{split}D_{2}^{A,0}&\equiv\frac{D_{2}^{\text{id}}}{D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}}\,,\qquad D_{2}^{A,\ell+j}\equiv D_{2}^{A_{\ell+1-j}}\,,\end{split}

(5.17)

for
j=1,..,\ell
.
The symmetry action on the vacua takes the form

D_{2}^{A_{p}}:\begin{pmatrix}v_{0}\\
v_{[j]}\end{pmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{pmatrix}v_{[j]}\\
v_{[j+p]}+v_{[j-p]}\end{pmatrix}\,,

(5.18)

where we have made the identifications
v_{[0]}\equiv 2v_{0}
and
v_{[\ell+j]}=v_{[\ell+1-j]}
.

•

\bm{n=2\ell}
: Now we construct the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell}^{(1)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB phase.
We start with the
D_{4\ell}
symmetric gapped phase that is the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell}
SSB Phase.
We present
D_{4\ell}
as

D_{4\ell}=\langle a\,,b\ |a^{2\ell}=b^{2}=1\,,bab=a^{2\ell-1}\rangle\,.

(5.19)

This phase has
2\ell
vacua, which we label as

v_{j}\,,\qquad j=-\ell+1\,,\dots\,,0\,,\dots\,,\ell\,.

(5.20)

All these states are cyclically permuted under the action of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell}
, hence this is the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell}
SSB phase.
Under the action of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
,
v_{0}
and
v_{\ell}
are invariant while
v_{j}
and
v_{-j}
are interchanged.
For example, the case of
\ell=3
has 6 vacua which realize the
D_{12}
symmetry as

(5.21)

From the perspective of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
symmetry, the ground states in this phase split as

{\rm Triv}_{0}\oplus{\rm Triv}_{\ell}\oplus\bigoplus_{j=1}^{\ell-1}{\rm Triv}_{\pm j}\,,

(5.22)

Therefore after gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
symmetry, one obtains a phase with
\ell+1
vacua, two of which are topologically ordered and
\ell-1
are topologically trivial.
The phase structure can be summarized as

2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell+1}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
:
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell+1}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
SSB Phase

The underlying 3d TFT is

\left[{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{t}\right]_{0}\ \bigoplus_{j=1}^{\ell}\ {\rm Triv}_{[j]}\ \bigoplus\ \left[{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{t}\right]_{\ell}\,.

(5.23)

(5.24)

The symmetry structure of the gauged theory is
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2\ell}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
which has a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry generated by
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
, an
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form symmetry generated by
D_{2}^{a^{\ell}}
and
\ell-1
non-invertible symmerty generators
D_{2}^{A_{p}}
which descend from
D_{2}^{a^{p}}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{-p}}
upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
.
The fusion rules among these symmetry generators is

\begin{split}D_{2}^{A_{p}}\otimes D_{2}^{a^{\ell}}&=D_{2}^{A_{\ell-p}}\,,\\
D_{2}^{A_{p}}\otimes D_{2}^{A_{p^{\prime}}}&=D_{2}^{A_{p+p^{\prime}}}\oplus D_{2}^{A_{p-p^{\prime}}}\,,\end{split}

(5.25)

where we use the identifications

D_{2}^{A_{0}}\equiv\frac{D_{2}^{\text{id}}}{D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}}\,,\quad D_{2}^{A_{\ell}}\equiv\frac{D_{2}^{a^{\ell}}}{D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}}\,,\quad D_{2}^{A_{\ell+j}}\equiv D_{2}^{A_{\ell-j}}\,,

(5.26)

Similarly, the action on the ground states is determined to be

\begin{split}D_{2}^{a^{\ell}}&:v_{0}\longleftrightarrow v_{\ell}\,,\\
&:v_{[j]}\longleftrightarrow v_{[\ell-j]}\,,\\
D_{2}^{A_{p}}&:v_{0}\longrightarrow v_{[j]}\,,\\
&:v_{[j]}\longrightarrow v_{[j+p]}+v_{[j-p]}\,,\end{split}

(5.27)

where we use the identifications
v_{[0]}\equiv 2v_{0}
,
v_{[\ell]}=2v_{\ell}
and
v_{[\ell+j]}=v_{[\ell-j]}
.

5.2
Non-minimal SSB Phases

The above discussion can be immediately generalized to non-minimal
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB phases.
For this, before gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, one considers a
D_{2n}
0-form symmetric phase which realizes a non-minimal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{n}
SPT.
This has
n
-vacua that are permuted by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(0)}
.
Either one or two vacua (depending on whether
n
is odd or even respectively) are invariant under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
while the remaining are organized into pairs that are mapped into each other under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
.
To construct the non-minimal
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{n}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
phase, we consider each of these vacua to be topologically ordered.
I.e., each vacuum effectively realizes a 3d TFT whose underlying category of lines is some fixed MTC
\mathcal{M}
.
The vacua that are
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
invariant have a certain
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry defined via choice of a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
extended braided fusion category
\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
.
Upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, these vacua map to vacua in which the dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry has been spontaneouly broken.
These are concretely obtained via the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
equivariantization of
\mathcal{M}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}^{\times}
.
The rest of the vacua realize topological orders
\mathcal{M}
after gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
.
